label: Arab Painting
defn: manuscript painting of the Arab lands from the 12th to the 15th century: illustrated scientific texts, the Maqamat of al-Hariri and Kalila wa Dimna, made in Baghdad, Mosul, Syria and Mamluk Egypt (al-Wasiti's 1237 Maqamat).
aliases: Arabic miniature; Baghdad school; Mesopotamian school

label: Persian Miniature
defn: Persian manuscript and album painting from the Mongol conquest to the 19th century, taught in court workshops whose schools are named after their centres (Herat, Tabriz, Qazvin, Isfahan, Shiraz, Bukhara); kinds are those schools and their masters (Bihzad, Sultan Muhammad, Riza-yi 'Abbasi).

label: Ottoman Miniature
defn: painting of the Ottoman court workshop (nakkaşhane) for histories, festival books and albums, from Mehmed II to the 18th century (Matrakçı Nasuh's topographies, Nakkaş Osman's Hünername, Levni's Surname-i Vehbi).

label: Mughal Painting
defn: painting of the Mughal court atelier and its offshoots in South Asia, 16th–19th century: the Hamzanama and the illustrated histories of Akbar, Jahangir's portraits and natural history, and the sub-imperial and provincial schools (Lucknow, Murshidabad).

label: Deccan Painting
defn: painting of the Deccan sultanates (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda) and of Hyderabad after them, 16th–19th century, with its lyrical colour and Persian, Turkman and Vijayanagara sources.

label: Company Painting
defn: paintings made by Indian artists for officials of the East India Company and other Europeans, 18th–19th century, in a hybrid of Mughal technique and European natural history and topography (Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, Murshidabad, Tanjore).

label: Rajput Painting
defn: Court painting of the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan and Central India, 16th–19th century, in schools named for their courts: Mewar Ragamala sets, Bundi and Kota hunting scenes, Kishangarh portraits of Radha, Jodhpur durbar paintings.

label: Pahari Painting
defn: Painting of the Hindu courts of the Punjab Hills, 17th–19th century, from the bold Basohli Rasamanjari to the lyrical Guler and Kangra Gita Govinda and Bhagavata Purana series of the family of Pandit Seu.

label: Jain Manuscript Painting
defn: The Western Indian style of manuscript painting on palm leaf and then paper (11th–16th century), chiefly Jain scriptures with angular figures and projecting far eyes: Kalpasutra, Kalakacharyakatha, painted wooden covers (patli).
aliases: Western Indian style;Jain painting;Western Indian painting

label: Sikh Painting
defn: Painting in the Punjab under Sikh patronage, late 18th–19th century, in Pahari and Company-influenced idioms: portraits of Ranjit Singh and his court, Janamsakhi illustrations, Gurus series.

label: Assamese Manuscript Painting
defn: Manuscript painting of Assam on sanchipat (agarwood-bark) folios, 16th–19th century, in sattriya and Ahom court styles: Hastividyarnava, illustrated Bhagavata.

label: Burmese Parabaik Painting
defn: Painting in watercolour on white parabaik (folding books of mulberry paper) by the royal and monastic painters of Konbaung Burma, 18th–19th century: court ceremonies and processions, Life of the Buddha, Jataka cycles, cosmologies.

label: Thai Manuscript Painting
defn: Paintings in gouache and gold on khoi-paper folding books of Siam, late 17th–19th century, chiefly funerary chanting books: Phra Malai manuscripts, Traiphum cosmologies, Ten Great Jatakas.
aliases: samut khoi painting;Phra Malai manuscript painting

label: Nara-ehon
defn: Illustrated books and scrolls of tales painted in bright mineral colours by largely anonymous town painters of Kyoto, late 16th–18th century: Tales of Ise, Bunshō zōshi, otogi-zōshi booklets.

label: Ethiopian Manuscript Painting
defn: Painting in Ethiopian Christian manuscripts on parchment, from the Aksumite-era gospel books to the Gondarine Marian miracle books: Garima Gospels evangelist portraits, Miracles of Mary (Täammərä Maryam) cycles, illustrated Psalters.

label: Byzantine Illuminated Manuscripts
defn: Painted miniatures in Greek manuscripts of the Byzantine empire, 4th–15th century, from late antique codices to the classicising Macedonian Renaissance and Palaiologan books: Vienna Dioscurides, Rossano Gospels, Paris Psalter, Menologion of Basil II.

label: Borgia Group
defn: The pre-Hispanic ritual and divinatory screenfold codices painted on deerskin in the Mixteca-Puebla style of central Mexico, 14th–early 16th century: Codex Borgia, Codex Laud, Codex Fejérváry-Mayer, Codex Cospi.

label: Mixtec Codices
defn: Genealogical and historical screenfold codices painted on deerskin by Mixtec (Ñudzavui) tlacuiloque of Oaxaca, 14th–16th century: Codex Zouche-Nuttall, Codex Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Codex Bodley, Codex Colombino.

label: Aztec Codices
defn: Pictorial manuscripts of the Nahua of central Mexico, from the few pre-Hispanic and early colonial ritual books to the colonial histories, tribute rolls and encyclopedias painted by indigenous tlacuiloque: Codex Borbonicus, Codex Mendoza, Florentine Codex, Codex Azcatitlan.

label: Armenian Manuscript Illumination
defn: Painting and ornament of Armenian Gospel books and service books from the 10th to the 18th century, taught in monastic schools named after their regions: Etchmiadzin Gospels, Mugni Gospels, Toros Roslin's Gospels, Glajor Gospels.

label: Gongbi
defn: The meticulous, finely outlined and coloured manner of Chinese court and academy painting from the Tang and Song: Emperor Huizong's Auspicious Cranes, Zhang Zeduan's Along the River during the Qingming Festival.

label: Northern Landscape Style
defn: The monumental landscape painting of the Five Dynasties and Northern Song: Fan Kuan's Travelers among Mountains and Streams, Guan Tong's Waiting for the Ferry.

label: Literati Painting
defn: Scholar-amateur painting of China (wenrenhua) and its Korean and Japanese reflexes, valuing brushwork, poetry and calligraphy over likeness: Ni Zan's Rongxi Studio, Huang Gongwang's Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains, Dong Qichang's landscapes.
aliases: Southern School;wenrenhua;scholar painting;Chinese landscape painting;shanshui;Chinese scroll painting

label: Zhe School
defn: The professional Ming school of landscape continuing Southern Song Ma–Xia painting (15th–16th century): Dai Jin's Returning Home Late from a Spring Outing, Wu Wei's figures.

label: Wu School
defn: The Ming literati school of Suzhou (15th–16th century) around Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming: Shen Zhou's Lofty Mount Lu, Wen Zhengming's Old Trees by a Cold Waterfall.

label: Shanghai School
defn: The commercial-literati painting of late Qing Shanghai, bold in colour and subject: Ren Bonian's portraits, Wu Changshuo's flowers.

label: Lingnan School
defn: The Cantonese school (early 20th century) of the Gao brothers and Chen Shuren that joined Chinese brushwork with Japanese and Western realism: Gao Jianfu's Flying in the Rain, Zhao Shao'ang's birds.

label: Yamato-e
defn: The classical Japanese narrative and court painting style from the Heian period, continued by the Tosa school: the Tale of Genji scrolls, the Shigisan engi emaki, Tosa Mitsuoki's Quail and Millet.

label: Kanō School
defn: The hereditary school of Japanese official painting (15th–19th century) joining Chinese ink and Yamato-e colour: Kanō Eitoku's Cypress Trees, Kanō Tan'yū's Nijō Castle screens.

label: Rinpa School
defn: The decorative Japanese school of Sōtatsu, Kōrin and Hōitsu (17th–19th century): Sōtatsu's Wind God and Thunder God, Kōrin's Irises.

label: Nanga
defn: Japanese literati painting (bunjinga) of the later Edo period and its Meiji continuation: Ike no Taiga and Yosa Buson's Ten Conveniences and Ten Pleasures, Uragami Gyokudō's Frozen Clouds.

label: Maruyama–Shijō School
defn: The naturalistic Kyoto painting of Maruyama Ōkyo and Matsumura Goshun (from the 1770s) and its modern heirs: Ōkyo's Pine Trees in Snow, Goshun's Woodcutters and Fishermen.

label: Nihonga
defn: Modern Japanese-style painting (from the 1880s) in mineral pigments and ink on silk and paper: Hishida Shunsō's Fallen Leaves, Yokoyama Taikan's works, Uemura Shōen's Flame.

label: Ink Wash Painting
defn: Monochrome ink painting of the Zen monasteries of Muromachi Japan (suibokuga), after Song and Yuan models: Mokuan Reien's Four Sleepers, Josetsu's Catching a Catfish with a Gourd, Sesshū's Landscape of the Four Seasons.

label: Ethiopian Icon Painting
defn: Panel painting of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church from the 15th century, in tempera on gessoed wood (later over glued cloth), as diptychs, triptychs and processional icons, in the styles named First and Second Gondarine: Virgin and Child with archangels, St George on horseback, Kwer'ata Re'esu.

label: Byzantine Icons
defn: Devotional images painted in encaustic or egg tempera on wooden panels in the Byzantine empire and its orbit, 6th–15th century: Sinai Christ Pantokrator, Theotokos of Vladimir, Hodegetria and Deesis icons.

label: Cretan School
defn: Post-Byzantine icon painting of Venetian Crete, 15th–17th century, joining the Palaiologan manner with Italian elements: icons of Andreas Ritzos and Michael Damaskinos, Theophanes the Cretan's Athonite murals.

label: Georgian Icon Painting
defn: Painted panel icons of medieval and early modern Georgia, from the 10th century, often set in chased silver revetments: icons of Svaneti, Gelati iconostasis, Georgian icons at Sinai.

label: Palaeologan Renaissance
defn: Late Byzantine painting (1261–1453), classicising and intensely expressive in icons and frescoes: the Chora Church frescoes, Theophanes the Greek's icons.

label: Russian Icons
defn: Icon painting of Rus' and Muscovy and its schools (Novgorod, Moscow, Vologda, Stroganov): Rublev's Trinity, Dionisius's Ferapontov icons.

label: Pattachitra
defn: Cloth-based painting of Odisha by the chitrakar community of Puri and Raghurajpur, in mineral colour on gum-and-chalk-primed cotton: Jagannath images, Gita Govinda panels, palm-leaf pothis.

label: Bengal Patachitra
defn: The narrative scroll painting of the patuas (chitrakars) of West Bengal and Bangladesh, unrolled frame by frame while the painter sings (pater gaan): Manasamangal scrolls, Jadupatua scrolls of the Santal.

label: Kalighat Painting
defn: Watercolours on mill paper sold by patua painters at the Kalighat temple in Calcutta, 19th–early 20th century, with bold outlines and satire of urban life: Durga and Kali icons, Tarakeswar scandal, babu and courtesan pictures.

label: Pichwai
defn: Large painted cloth hangings made at Nathdwara to hang behind the image of Shrinathji: Sharad Purnima, Annakut, cows and lotus ponds.

label: Mata ni Pachedi
defn: Ritual cloth shrines of the Vaghri community of Ahmedabad, hand-painted and block-printed in red and black around the Mother Goddess: Mata on her vahana, temple cloth panels.

label: Cheriyal Scroll Painting
defn: Narrative scrolls of Cheriyal in Telangana painted for the bardic storytellers of the Kaki Padagollu: Markandeya Purana scrolls, Gauda Purana.

label: Thangka
defn: Buddhist painting on cotton or silk mounted in a textile frame to be hung, rolled and carried, the principal portable painting of Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh and Mongolia: deity and lineage portraits, mandalas, wheel-of-life paintings, appliqué festival thangkas.

label: Beri
defn: The Newar-derived style of Tibetan painting (13th–15th century) and its later continuations, with dense red and blue grounds and Nepalese figure canons: Sakya lineage thangkas, Ngor mandala sets.

label: Menri
defn: The central Tibetan painting tradition founded by Menla Döndrub (15th century), with Chinese-inspired landscape and a canon of peaceful deities, renewed as New Menri by Choying Gyatso at Tashi Lhunpo (17th century): arhat sets, lineage paintings.

label: Khyenri
defn: The central Tibetan painting style created by Khyentse Chenmo of Gongkar Chöde (15th century), known for wrathful deities, bright palettes and near-circular haloes: Gongkar Chöde murals, wrathful protector thangkas.

label: Karma Gadri
defn: The 'encampment' painting tradition of the Karma Kagyu, founded by Namkha Tashi (16th century) and renewed by Situ Panchen at Palpung (18th century), with open Chinese-style landscapes and pale grounds: Situ Panchen's Eight Great Mahasiddhas, Tenth Karmapa paintings.

label: Regong Arts
defn: The thangka painting (with murals, sculpture and appliqué) of the monastic artists of Rebkong (Tongren) in Amdo, from the 17th century to the present, on UNESCO's list since 2009: Wutun monastery thangkas, contemporary Rebkong painting.

label: Paubha
defn: Newar Buddhist and Hindu painting on cloth of the Kathmandu Valley, from the 12th century to the present, with flat red grounds and donor registers: Vasudhara mandalas, Chakrasamvara paubhas, long narrative vratha paintings.

label: Dunhuang Paintings
defn: The portable Buddhist paintings and banners on silk, hemp and paper deposited in the Library Cave (Cave 17) at the Mogao Caves, 8th–10th century: Tejaprabha and the Five Planets (897), bodhisattva banners, Famous Images of the Buddha.

label: Kamasan Painting
defn: The classical wayang-style painting of Kamasan village in Klungkung, Bali, on cloth and bark paper for temples and palaces since the Gelgel court (16th century): ider-ider friezes, langse hangings, palelintangan calendars, Kerta Gosa ceilings.
aliases: Kamasan wayang painting;wayang style painting;sangging Kamasan

label: Wayang Beber
defn: Javanese narrative scroll painting on dluwang bark paper, unrolled scene by scene by a dalang: Panji scrolls of Pacitan and Gunung Kidul.

label: Ethiopian Magic Scrolls
defn: Protective parchment scrolls cut to the owner's height and painted by däbtära (church-trained scholars) with talismanic figures, eyes, angels and nets beside Ge'ez prayers: healing scrolls, talismanic eyes and faces, Solomon's net designs.

label: Plains Hide Painting
defn: Painting on tanned or raw hide by the peoples of the Great Plains: men's figurative war-exploit and calendar painting and women's geometric designs, on painted buffalo robes, tipi covers and liners, parfleches and winter counts.

label: Qajar Painting
defn: court painting of Qajar Iran (1789–1925) in oil on canvas and in watercolour: life-size royal portraits and figures of pleasure (Mihr 'Ali), and the realist watercolours of Abu'l-Hasan Ghaffari (Sani' al-Mulk).

label: Balinese Painting
defn: The modern painting of Bali from the late 1920s on paper and canvas, in the village schools that grew up around the Pita Maha association: Ubud genre and landscape, Batuan dense ink-and-wash scenes, Lempad's line drawings.

label: Sơn Mài
defn: Vietnamese lacquer painting on panel, developed as a fine art at the École des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine from the 1930s: landscape and genre panels, gold- and eggshell-inlaid screens.

label: Fayum Mummy Portraits
defn: Portraits painted in encaustic or tempera on wooden panels and bound over the faces of mummies in Roman Egypt, 1st–3rd century: Hawara and Er-Rubayat portraits, Tomb of Aline, portraits from Antinoöpolis.

label: New Spanish Baroque
defn: The painting of the Viceroyalty of New Spain in the Baroque idiom, 17th–18th century, from the large altarpieces and sacristy canvases of Mexico City to devotional and civic pictures: Villalpando's Puebla cathedral dome, Juan Correa's sacristy canvases, Miguel Cabrera's Virgins of Guadalupe.

label: Casta Painting
defn: Sets of paintings made in 18th-century New Spain (and occasionally Peru) depicting the hierarchy of racial mixtures as family groups with their dress and produce: Miguel Cabrera's casta series (1763), José de Páez series.

label: Enconchado
defn: Paintings of late 17th- and early 18th-century New Spain in oil on panel with inlaid fragments of mother-of-pearl under translucent glazes, influenced by Japanese namban lacquer: González family Conquest of Mexico series, Virgin of Guadalupe (1698).

label: Biombo
defn: Painted folding screens made in New Spain from the early 17th century after Japanese byōbu, with views of Mexico City, the Conquest and festivities: Biombo of the Conquest and View of Mexico City, Indian wedding and flying pole screen.

label: Cusco School
defn: The school of religious painting centred on Cusco in the Viceroyalty of Peru, 16th–18th century, with Andean painters working from Flemish prints and adding brocade gold (brocateado) and local flora: Corpus Christi series, archangel arquebusiers, Diego Quispe Tito's zodiac series.

label: Potosí School
defn: The school of painting of the silver city of Potosí in Upper Peru (Bolivia), 17th–18th century, led by Melchor Pérez de Holguín: Entry of Viceroy Morcillo into Potosí, Virgin of the Cerro.

label: Quito School
defn: The painting and polychrome sculpture of the Audiencia of Quito, 16th–18th century, known for its realist carved and estofado images and its painting workshops: Miguel de Santiago's Augustinian series, Legarda's winged Virgin of Quito, Caspicara's sculptural groups.

label: Western Desert Painting
defn: The acrylic painting movement of the Central and Western Desert begun at Papunya in 1971, in which Dreaming (Tjukurrpa/Jukurrpa) designs once made in sand, body paint and ceremony are painted on canvas and board in dotted and concentric-circle fields, carried on by community art centres: Papunya Tul
aliases: Western Desert art movement;dot painting;Papunya Tula painting;acrylic desert painting

label: Contemporary Indigenous Australian Art
defn: Painting by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists from the 1970s onward outside the Western Desert and bark-painting lineages, in ochre and acrylic on canvas, worked through community art centres: Warmun (Turkey Creek) ochre paintings, Mangkaja and Ngukurr acrylics, Mornington Island paintin

label: Hermannsburg School
defn: The Western Arrernte watercolour landscape school of the Hermannsburg mission (from 1934), founded by Albert Namatjira after lessons with Rex Battarbee and carried on by his family and followers: MacDonnell Ranges landscapes, ghost gums.

label: Romanesque Painting
defn: Panel, book and wall painting of Latin Europe in the 11th–12th centuries, with flat, linear, hieratic figures: the Master of Pedret, painted altar frontals of Catalonia, the Registrum Gregorii.

label: Gothic Painting
defn: Painting in Latin Europe from the 13th to the late 14th century, from Italo-Byzantine panel crosses to the narrative altarpieces of Giotto and his followers: Coppo di Marcovaldo's crucifixes, Giotto's Ognissanti Madonna, Catalan Gothic retables.

label: Sienese School
defn: The school of painting of Siena, 13th–15th century, with its gold grounds, lyrical line and colour: Duccio's Maestà, Simone Martini's Annunciation, Lorenzetti's Allegory of Good Government.

label: International Gothic
defn: The courtly late Gothic style shared by painters across Europe c. 1375–1425, elegant, decorative and richly detailed: the Wilton Diptych, Gentile da Fabriano's Adoration of the Magi, the Très Riches Heures.

label: Early Netherlandish Painting
defn: Oil painting of the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands in the 15th and early 16th centuries, with minute naturalism and luminous glazes: the Ghent Altarpiece, the Arnolfini Portrait, Rogier van der Weyden's Descent from the Cross.

label: Italian Renaissance Painting
defn: Painting in Italy c. 1400–1530, from the perspective and naturalism of the Florentine Early Renaissance to the High Renaissance: Masaccio's Trinity, Piero della Francesca's Flagellation, Leonardo's Last Supper, Raphael's School of Athens.

label: Venetian School
defn: The painting of Venice and its terraferma from the Bellini to the 18th century, built on colour and light: Giovanni Bellini's San Zaccaria Altarpiece, Giorgione's Tempest, Titian's Assumption, Veronese's Wedding at Cana.

label: Northern Renaissance
defn: The Renaissance north of the Alps (German lands, the Low Countries, France, England), c. 1490–1580: Dürer's Self-Portrait of 1500, the Isenheim Altarpiece, Holbein's Ambassadors, Bruegel's Hunters in the Snow.
aliases: German Renaissance;Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painting;French Renaissance

label: Mannerism
defn: The artificial, elongated and complex style that followed the High Renaissance, c. 1520–1600: Pontormo's Deposition, Parmigianino's Madonna with the Long Neck, Bronzino's Allegory with Venus and Cupid.

label: School of Fontainebleau
defn: The Mannerist decoration and painting of the French court at Fontainebleau, led by Rosso and Primaticcio (c. 1530–1610): the Galerie François I, Gabrielle d'Estrées and One of Her Sisters.

label: Baroque Painting
defn: European painting of the 17th and early 18th centuries, dramatic in light, movement and emotion, from Rome to Madrid and the colonial Americas: Rubens's Elevation of the Cross, Velázquez's Las Meninas, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling.

label: Caravaggisti
defn: Followers of Caravaggio's dramatic tenebrism and naturalism across Europe, c. 1600–1640: Gentileschi's Judith Slaying Holofernes, Ter Brugghen's Calling of Saint Matthew, Valentin de Boulogne's Concert.

label: Flemish Baroque Painting
defn: Painting of the Southern Netherlands c. 1585–1700 around Rubens, van Dyck and Jordaens: Rubens's Descent from the Cross, van Dyck's Charles I at the Hunt, Snyders's market stalls.

label: Dutch Golden Age Painting
defn: Painting of the Dutch Republic in the 17th century, its genres sold on an open market: Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's View of Delft, Ruisdael's Jewish Cemetery, Heda's breakfast pieces.

label: Rococo
defn: The light, ornamental, intimate style of the 18th century, from the French fêtes galantes to Venetian ceilings: Watteau's Pilgrimage to Cythera, Fragonard's The Swing, Tiepolo's Würzburg ceiling.

label: Neoclassicism
defn: Painting of the later 18th and early 19th century modelled on antiquity, severe in line and moral in subject: David's Oath of the Horatii, Mengs's Parnassus, Ingres's Grande Odalisque.

label: Romanticism
defn: Painting c. 1780–1850 that put feeling, the sublime and the imagination before rule: Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, Géricault's Raft of the Medusa, Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People, Turner's Slave Ship.

label: Nazarene Movement
defn: German Romantic painters in Rome (from 1809) who revived the religious art of Dürer and early Raphael: Overbeck's Italia and Germania, the Casa Bartholdy frescoes.

label: Danish Golden Age
defn: Danish painting of the first half of the 19th century, around Eckersberg and his pupils: Købke's View of Lake Sortedam, Eckersberg's views of Rome.

label: Düsseldorf School of Painting
defn: Painters trained at the Düsseldorf Academy c. 1819–1918, known for detailed landscapes and history scenes: Achenbach's seascapes, Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware.

label: Barbizon School
defn: French landscape painters working from nature in the forest of Fontainebleau c. 1830–1870: Rousseau's Forest of Fontainebleau, Millet's The Gleaners, Corot's Souvenir de Mortefontaine.

label: Hudson River School
defn: American Romantic landscape painting c. 1825–1875: Cole's The Oxbow, Church's Heart of the Andes, Bierstadt's Rocky Mountains.

label: Norwich School of Painters
defn: The regional landscape school of Norwich (1803–1833) around John Crome and John Sell Cotman: Crome's Mousehold Heath, Cotman's Greta Bridge.

label: Academic Art
defn: Painting shaped by the European academies and their Salons in the 19th century, finished, idealising and hierarchical in subject: Cabanel's Birth of Venus, Bouguereau's Nymphs and Satyr, Gérôme's Pollice Verso.

label: Neo-Grec
defn: A mid-19th-century French current of small-scale, archaeologically detailed antique genre scenes: Gérôme's Cock Fight, Hamon's My Sister Is Not In.

label: Realism
defn: The mid-19th-century movement that painted contemporary life and labour without idealisation: Courbet's A Burial at Ornans, Millet's The Angelus, Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga.

label: Costumbrismo
defn: Spanish and Latin American painting of local customs, types and manners in the 19th century: Bécquer's Andalusian scenes, Pancho Fierro's Lima watercolours.

label: Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
defn: The English brotherhood (1848) and its circle that painted with the detail and colour of art before Raphael: Millais's Ophelia, Rossetti's Beata Beatrix, Hunt's The Light of the World.

label: Hague School
defn: Dutch painters working in The Hague c. 1860–1900 in grey-toned realist landscape and genre: Mesdag's Panorama, Mauve's Morning Ride on the Beach.

label: Macchiaioli
defn: Tuscan painters of the 1850s–1870s who built pictures from patches (macchie) of light and shade: Fattori's The Rotonda di Palmieri, Lega's The Visit.

label: Naturalism
defn: Late-19th-century plein-air painting of rural and working life with photographic truth: Bastien-Lepage's Haymaking, Stanhope Forbes's A Fish Sale on a Cornish Beach, the Skagen Painters.

label: Munich School
defn: Painters trained at the Munich Academy c. 1850–1914 in dark, painterly realism: Leibl's Three Women in Church, Gyzis's works, Chase's early portraits.

label: Impressionism
defn: The French movement of the 1860s–1880s that painted modern life and light in broken colour outdoors, and its national offshoots: Monet's Impression, Sunrise, Renoir's Bal du moulin de la Galette, Morisot's The Cradle.

label: Neo-Impressionism
defn: The systematic colour-division of Seurat and Signac from 1886 and its Italian divisionist branch: Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Signac's Portrait of Félix Fénéon.

label: Post-Impressionism
defn: Painting after Impressionism c. 1886–1905 that turned colour and form to structure and expression: Cézanne's Mont Sainte-Victoire, Van Gogh's Starry Night, Gauguin's Vision after the Sermon.

label: Pont-Aven School
defn: Painters around Gauguin and Émile Bernard in Brittany from 1886, flat colour and bounding line (synthetism, cloisonnism): Bernard's Breton Women in the Meadow, Sérusier's The Talisman.

label: Symbolism
defn: Late-19th-century painting of dream, myth and inner states: Moreau's The Apparition, Redon's The Cyclops, Khnopff's I Lock My Door Upon Myself.

label: Aestheticism
defn: The British "art for art's sake" painting of the 1860s–1890s: Whistler's Symphony in White, Leighton's Flaming June, Albert Moore's Midsummer.

label: Tonalism
defn: American (and Australian) landscape painting c. 1880–1915 in muted, atmospheric tones: Inness's Home of the Heron, Dewing's The Recitation.

label: Luminism
defn: American landscape painting c. 1850–1875 of calm, hidden-brushwork light: Fitz Henry Lane's Owl's Head, Heade's Approaching Thunder Storm.

label: Glasgow School
defn: The Glasgow Boys (c. 1880–1900), Scottish painters of plein-air naturalism and decorative colour: Guthrie's A Highland Funeral, Henry and Hornel's The Druids.

label: Expressionism
defn: Painting from c. 1905 that distorted colour and form for emotional force, centred in Germany and Austria: Kirchner's Street, Berlin, Kokoschka's The Bride of the Wind, Marc's Blue Horse.

label: Fauvism
defn: The French painting of pure, arbitrary colour around Matisse and Derain, 1904–1908: Matisse's Woman with a Hat, Derain's Charing Cross Bridge.

label: Cubism
defn: The movement of Picasso and Braque (from 1907) that fractured objects into planes and multiple viewpoints, with its Salon Cubist and Section d'Or circles: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Braque's Violin and Candlestick, Gris's Portrait of Picasso.

label: Futurism
defn: The Italian movement (1909) celebrating speed, machines and the city, and its Russian Cubo-Futurist branch: Boccioni's The City Rises, Balla's Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash, Severini's Armoured Train.

label: Orphism
defn: Abstract painting of prismatic colour around Robert and Sonia Delaunay and Kupka, c. 1912: Robert Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows, Kupka's Amorpha.

label: Vorticism
defn: The British avant-garde of 1914–1915 around Wyndham Lewis and the magazine BLAST: Bomberg's The Mud Bath, Lewis's The Crowd.

label: Suprematism
defn: Malevich's abstraction of pure geometric forms from 1915: Black Square, Suprematist Composition: White on White.

label: Constructivism
defn: The Russian movement from c. 1915 of art as construction and production, and its international heirs: Tatlin's Monument to the Third International, Rodchenko's Pure Colours, El Lissitzky's Proun.

label: De Stijl
defn: The Dutch movement (1917) of Neoplasticism, reducing art to primaries and the right angle: Mondrian's Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow, van Doesburg's Counter-Composition.

label: Dada
defn: The anti-art movement born in Zurich in 1916 and spread to Berlin, Paris and New York: Duchamp's Fountain, Höch's Cut with the Kitchen Knife, Arp's collages.

label: Surrealism
defn: The movement launched by Breton in 1924 that painted dream and the unconscious: Dalí's The Persistence of Memory, Magritte's The Treachery of Images, Ernst's Europe after the Rain.

label: Metaphysical Painting
defn: Giorgio de Chirico's and Carrà's painting of uncanny piazzas and mannequins, 1910–1920: The Disquieting Muses, Mystery and Melancholy of a Street.

label: New Objectivity
defn: The sober, sharp-focus realism of Weimar Germany in the 1920s: Dix's Portrait of Sylvia von Harden, Grosz's Pillars of Society, Schad's Self-Portrait with Model.

label: Magic Realism
defn: Realist painting of the 1920s–1950s that makes the everyday strange: Carel Willink's Wilma, Pyke Koch's Shooting Gallery, Ivan Albright's The Picture of Dorian Gray.

label: Precisionism
defn: American painting of the 1920s–1930s rendering industry and the city in crisp geometric planes: Sheeler's American Landscape, Demuth's My Egypt.

label: Regionalism
defn: American painting of the 1930s of the rural Midwest: Wood's American Gothic, Benton's America Today, Curry's Tragic Prelude.

label: Ashcan School
defn: New York realist painters of the early 20th century who depicted the city's streets and poor: Bellows's Stag at Sharkey's, Sloan's McSorley's Bar.

label: Social Realism
defn: Politically engaged realist painting of the 1920s–1940s on labour and poverty: Ben Shahn's The Passion of Sacco and Vanzetti, Isabel Bishop's working women.

label: Socialist Realism
defn: The official style of the Soviet Union from 1932 and of the socialist states: Gerasimov's Lenin on the Tribune, Deineka's Defence of Petrograd.

label: Harlem Renaissance
defn: The flowering of African-American art in the 1920s–1930s centred in Harlem: Aaron Douglas's Aspects of Negro Life, Archibald Motley's Nightlife, Augusta Savage's The Harp.

label: School of Paris
defn: The international, often émigré artists working in Paris c. 1900–1940 outside a single movement: Modigliani's Jeanne Hébuterne, Chagall's I and the Village, Soutine's Carcass of Beef.

label: Scuola Romana
defn: Roman painters of the 1920s–1930s around Scipione and Mafai, expressionist in colour against the classicising Novecento: Mafai's Demolitions, Scipione's Cardinal Decano.

label: Neo-Romanticism
defn: Figurative painting of the 1930s–1950s (Berman, Tchelitchew; the British Neo-Romantics) reviving Romantic landscape and mood: Paul Nash's Totes Meer, Sutherland's Entrance to a Lane.

label: Naïve Art
defn: Painting by artists without academic training, flat, detailed and frontal: Henri Rousseau's The Dream, Séraphine Louis's Tree of Paradise, Ivan Generalić's Hlebine paintings.

label: Art Brut
defn: Dubuffet's "raw art" of outsiders, the untrained and the institutionalised, and its successor outsider art: Adolf Wölfli's illustrated books, Aloïse Corbaz's theatres.

label: Abstract Expressionism
defn: The New York painting of the 1940s–1950s, gestural or field-based: Pollock's Autumn Rhythm, de Kooning's Woman I, Kline's Chief.

label: Color Field
defn: Abstraction of large expanses of flat or stained colour from the late 1940s: Rothko's No. 61 (Rust and Blue), Frankenthaler's Mountains and Sea, Newman's Vir Heroicus Sublimis.

label: Lyrical Abstraction
defn: Post-war gestural abstraction in Paris (abstraction lyrique) and its American 1960s sense: Georges Mathieu's Capetians Everywhere, Zao Wou-Ki's large canvases.

label: Informalism
defn: European post-war abstraction of matter, sign and gesture (art informel, tachisme, matter painting): Fautrier's Hostages, Wols's It's All Over, Tàpies's matter paintings.

label: COBRA
defn: The Copenhagen–Brussels–Amsterdam movement (1948–1951) of spontaneous, childlike expressionist painting: Appel's Questioning Children, Jorn's Letter to My Son.

label: Hard-edge Painting
defn: Abstraction of crisp-edged flat colour areas from the late 1950s: Ellsworth Kelly's Red Blue Green, Karl Benjamin's compositions.

label: Concrete Art
defn: Geometric abstraction built from pure plastic means, after van Doesburg's 1930 manifesto, in Switzerland, Italy and Latin America: Max Bill's Endless Ribbon, Lygia Clark's Bichos, Tomás Maldonado's works.

label: Op Art
defn: Abstraction of the 1960s exploiting optical effects: Bridget Riley's Movement in Squares, Vasarely's Vega series.

label: Pop Art
defn: Art of the late 1950s–1960s drawn from mass media, advertising and consumer goods: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans, Lichtenstein's Whaam!, Hamilton's Just What Is It ....

label: Neo-Dada
defn: American art of the late 1950s reviving Dada assemblage and found imagery: Rauschenberg's Monogram, Johns's Flag.

label: Nouveau Réalisme
defn: The French movement founded in 1960 around Restany, appropriating the real (décollage, accumulation, wrapping): Arman's Accumulations, Yves Klein's Anthropometries, Villeglé's torn posters.

label: Funk Art
defn: Irreverent figurative art of the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1960s, often in ceramics: Robert Arneson's self-portrait busts, Roy De Forest's paintings.

label: Bay Area Figurative Movement
defn: San Francisco painters of the 1950s–1960s who returned from abstraction to the figure: Diebenkorn's Cityscape I, David Park's Four Men.

label: Northwest School
defn: Painters of the Pacific Northwest in the 1930s–1950s, mystical and Asian-influenced: Mark Tobey's white writing, Morris Graves's Blind Bird.

label: Pattern and Decoration
defn: The American movement of the mid-1970s that reclaimed ornament, textile and craft: Miriam Schapiro's femmages, Robert Kushner's costumes.

label: Photorealism
defn: Painting from the late 1960s that reproduces photographs with exacting fidelity: Richard Estes's storefronts, Chuck Close's Big Self-Portrait.

label: Neo-figurative
defn: The return to the figure in 1960s Latin America and Spain (Otra Figuración): Jorge de la Vega's works, Luis Felipe Noé's Introduction to Hope.

label: Neo-Expressionism
defn: Figurative, expressive painting of the late 1970s–1980s: Baselitz's upside-down figures, Kiefer's Margarethe, Basquiat's Untitled (Skull).

label: Lettrism
defn: Isidore Isou's movement (from 1945) of letters and signs as the material of poetry and painting: Isou's hypergraphic novels, Lemaître's works.

label: Black Arts Movement
defn: The African-American art movement of 1965–1975 tied to Black Power (AfriCOBRA, the Wall of Respect): Jeff Donaldson's Wives of Shango, Wadsworth Jarrell's Revolutionary.

label: British Black Arts Movement
defn: Black British artists of the 1980s (the BLK Art Group) addressing race and diaspora: Lubaina Himid's A Fashionable Marriage, Keith Piper's works.

label: Lowbrow
defn: Californian pop-surrealist painting from the late 1970s rooted in comics, hot-rod and tattoo culture: Robert Williams's paintings, Mark Ryden's The Meat Show.

label: Mission School
defn: San Francisco artists of the 1990s working from street, folk and graffiti culture: Barry McGee's installations, Margaret Kilgallen's murals.

label: Stuckism
defn: The figurative painting movement founded in London in 1999 against conceptual art: Charles Thomson's Sir Nicholas Serota Makes an Acquisitions Decision.

label: Superflat
defn: Takashi Murakami's Japanese postmodern movement (2000) of flat anime and print-derived imagery: Murakami's Tan Tan Bo, Aya Takano's paintings.

label: Hurufiyya Movement
defn: Modern art of the Arab world and Iran (from the 1950s) that uses Arabic letters as abstract form: Madiha Omar's works, Shakir Hassan Al Said's The Contemplative Dimension, Parviz Tanavoli's Heech.

label: Dakar School
defn: Senegalese painting of the 1960s–1970s fostered by Senghor's Négritude policy: Papa Ibra Tall's tapestries, Iba N'Diaye's works.

label: Yōga
defn: Japanese painting in Western oil technique from the Meiji period: Kuroda Seiki's Lakeside, Takahashi Yuichi's Salmon, Kishida Ryūsei's Reiko.

label: Bengal School of Art
defn: The Indian nationalist painting movement of Abanindranath Tagore and his pupils (c. 1900–1940) reviving Mughal and Ajanta idioms: Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata, Nandalal Bose's Haripura posters.

label: Modern Art
defn: Painters born c. 1860–1944 active in Europe (and a few in the Americas) whose work is modern but who belong to no movement with its own leaf here; artists of a named movement (Fauvism, Cubism, Expressionism, Surrealism, Vienna Secession, Novecento Italiano, St Ives School ...) are listed in that lea

label: Contemporary Art
defn: The period style of painters and artists born from about 1945 who work after modernism in plural, global practices: post-colonial figurative painting, new abstraction, appropriation, art of the biennial circuit. Artists who belong to a named post-1945 movement (Neo-expressionism, Young British Artis

label: Hispano-Flemish Style
defn: Fifteenth-century painting of Castile and Aragon shaped by Early Netherlandish oil technique and realism, under the patronage of Isabella I: Bartolomé Bermejo's Saint Michael Triumphant, Fernando Gallego's Pietà, Pedro Berruguete's altarpieces.

label: Dansaekhwa
defn: The Korean monochrome painting movement of the 1970s: Park Seo-bo's Ecriture, Yun Hyong-keun's Umber-Blue, Chung Sang-hwa's grids, Ha Chong-hyun's Conjunction.

label: Orientalism
defn: Western painting of North Africa, the Ottoman lands, the Middle East and India, c. 1780–1914, from travel sketches to Salon harem and street scenes: Delacroix's Women of Algiers, Gérôme's The Snake Charmer, Lewis's The Hhareem. Membership: painters known chiefly for such subjects (or tagged Oriental

label: Peredvizhniki
defn: The Russian realist artists' cooperative (Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions, 1870–1923) that toured exhibitions of national genre, history and landscape painting: Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga, Savrasov's The Rooks Have Come Back, Surikov's Boyarynya Morozova. Membership: members or regula

label: Skagen Painters
defn: The Scandinavian artists' colony at Skagen in northern Jutland, c. 1875–1910, painting fishermen, beaches and the summer light: Krøyer's Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach, Michael Ancher's Will He Round the Point?. Membership: painters who worked at Skagen as part of the colony.

label: Newlyn School
defn: The colony of plein-air naturalist painters at Newlyn and Lamorna in Cornwall, from c. 1882: Stanhope Forbes's A Fish Sale on a Cornish Beach, Langley's Never Morning Wore to Evening, Bramley's A Hopeless Dawn. Membership: painters who settled or worked at Newlyn as part of the colony.

label: Lyon School
defn: The school of painting of Lyon, from the Troubadour painters around Révoil and Richard to the religious and idealist painters of the July Monarchy and Second Empire: Révoil's Joan of Arc in Prison, Janmot's The Poem of the Soul, Orsel's Good and Evil. Membership: painters trained at or working from

label: Golden Age of Finnish Art
defn: Finnish painting of c. 1880–1910, from Paris-trained naturalism to national romanticism and the Kalevala: Edelfelt's Conveying the Child's Coffin, Gallen-Kallela's The Defence of the Sampo, Schjerfbeck's The Convalescent. Membership: Finnish painters active in that generation.

label: Young British Artists
defn: Loose group of artists, many from Goldsmiths College, who showed together from the Freeze exhibition (London, 1988) and were collected by Charles Saatchi, culminating in Sensation (Royal Academy, 1997): Hirst, Emin, Lucas, Whiteread, the Chapman brothers, Ofili, Gordon.

label: Pictures Generation
defn: American artists of the late 1970s–80s, named after Douglas Crimp's Pictures exhibition (Artists Space, New York, 1977), who used appropriation, montage and photography to examine mass-media images: Sherrie Levine, Richard Prince, Barbara Kruger, Robert Longo, Cindy Sherman.

label: Mir iskusstva
defn: The St Petersburg World of Art society and magazine (1898–1904, revived 1910–1924) around Benois, Bakst and Diaghilev: retrospective, graphic and theatrical art. Members only: Somov, Lanceray, Golovin, Ostroumova-Lebedeva, Bilibin, Kustodiev, Roerich, Dobuzhinsky.

label: St Ives School
defn: Artists working in and around St Ives, Cornwall: the Victorian–Edwardian marine and landscape colony (Olsson, Talmage), and the modernists who gathered there from 1939 around Ben Nicholson and Barbara Hepworth (Lanyon, Heron, Hilton, Frost, Wynter, Barns-Graham).

label: Camden Town Group
defn: The London group of Post-Impressionist painters formed in 1911 around Walter Sickert at 19 Fitzroy Street (Gore, Gilman, Ginner, Bevan, Drummond, Manson, Lightfoot, Innes), with the women of the Fitzroy Street Group who were barred from membership (Sands, Gosse, Lessore).

label: ZERO
defn: The ZERO movement of light, motion and monochrome (1957–1966): the Düsseldorf ZERO group (Mack, Piene, Uecker), the Dutch Nul group, the Milan Azimut/h circle (Castellani, Manzoni) and Belgian and French associates.

label: Leipzig School
defn: The figurative painting school of the Leipzig Academy of Visual Arts in the German Democratic Republic: the founding generation (Heisig, Tübke, Mattheuer, Sitte) and their students (Rink, Stelzmann, Zander). Not the post-1990 New Leipzig School.

label: Nazi art
defn: Officially sanctioned art of the Third Reich (1933–1945): painters shown and bought at the Great German Art Exhibitions in Munich (Ziegler, Wissel, Peiner, Eichhorst, Saliger), and designers of party imagery. Membership test: work defined by the regime's cultural policy.

label: Vienna Secession
defn: The Union of Austrian Artists founded in 1897 by Klimt, Moser, Moll, Olbrich and Hoffmann, its exhibitions in the Secession building, and the Wiener Werkstätte workshops (1903–1932) that grew from it.

label: Novecento Italiano
defn: The Milan movement of a modern classical 'return to order' founded in 1922 by Margherita Sarfatti with seven painters (Bucci, Dudreville, Funi, Malerba, Marussig, Oppi, Sironi) and widened in the national exhibitions of 1926 and 1929 (Tosi, Carena, Campigli, Martini).

label: Modernisme
defn: Catalan modernism in painting, c. 1888–1911: Rusiñol and Casas's Sitges festivals, the Els Quatre Gats tavern circle and the Colla del Safrà, and the decorative painters of Barcelona. Architecture of the movement sits under Art Nouveau Architecture.

label: Noucentisme
defn: The Catalan cultural movement of a Mediterranean classicism (c. 1906–1923) named by Eugeni d'Ors, reacting against Modernisme: Sunyer, Torres-García, Togores, Galí, Obiols, the sculptors Clarà and Manolo Hugué.

label: Soviet nonconformist art
defn: Unofficial art made in the Soviet Union outside Socialist Realism, c. 1953–1986: the Lianozovo group, Moscow Conceptualism, Sots Art, the Dvizhenie kinetic group and independent Moscow and Leningrad artists.

label: Nagybánya artists' colony
defn: The plein-air painters' colony founded in 1896 at Nagybánya (Baia Mare) by Hollósy, Ferenczy, Réti, Thorma and Iványi-Grünwald, the cradle of Hungarian modern painting, including the 'Neos' who became The Eight.

label: Young Poland
defn: Polish modernism c. 1890–1918, centred on Kraków: Symbolist and Art Nouveau painters of the Society of Polish Artists 'Sztuka' (Malczewski, Wyspiański, Mehoffer, Stanisławski, Boznańska) and its sculptors and designers.

label: Kraków Group
defn: The Kraków avant-garde association founded in 1932 and re-founded in 1957 around Tadeusz Kantor, Maria Jarema and Jonasz Stern: abstraction, Informel and theatre.

label: Gutai group
defn: Members of the Gutai Art Association (Gutai Bijutsu Kyōkai), founded by Jirō Yoshihara in Ashiya in 1954 and dissolved in 1972: e.g. Kazuo Shiraga, Saburō Murakami, Atsuko Tanaka, Sadamasa Motonaga.

label: Group of Seven (artists)
defn: Members of the Group of Seven, the Toronto landscape painters who exhibited together from 1920 to 1931 (enlarged to ten members): e.g. Lawren Harris, A. Y. Jackson, Frederick Varley, A. J. Casson.

label: Brazilian modernism
defn: Brazilian modernist artists from the 1917 Malfatti exhibition and the Semana de Arte Moderna (1922) to the 1940s, including the Antropofagia circle and the São Paulo and Rio groups (Grupo Santa Helena, Núcleo Bernardelli): e.g. Tarsila do Amaral, Di Cavalcanti, Candido Portinari.

label: Progressive Artists' Group
defn: Members and close associates of the Progressive Artists' Group founded in Bombay in 1947 by F. N. Souza: e.g. S. H. Raza, M. F. Husain, K. H. Ara, Akbar Padamsee.

label: Generación de la Ruptura
defn: Mexican artists of the 1950s–60s who broke with the Mexican School and muralism in favour of abstraction and new figuration: e.g. José Luis Cuevas, Manuel Felguérez, Lilia Carrillo, Vicente Rojo.

label: Indigenismo
defn: Andean indigenista painters and sculptors of c. 1920–1960 who made Indigenous people and landscape the subject of a national modern art: e.g. José Sabogal (Peru), Camilo Egas (Ecuador), Cecilio Guzmán de Rojas (Bolivia). (Mexican indigenist muralists sit under Mexican Muralism.)

label: Chicago Imagists
defn: Chicago figurative artists shown at the Hyde Park Art Center 1966–1971 (Hairy Who, False Image, Nonplussed Some), with their teachers and the Monster Roster precursors: e.g. Jim Nutt, Gladys Nilsson, Roger Brown, Ed Paschke.

label: Feminist art movement
defn: Artists of the feminist art movement of the late 1960s–1980s, centred in the United States (A.I.R. Gallery, Heresies, the Feminist Art Program): e.g. Judy Chicago, Nancy Spero, Harmony Hammond, Mary Beth Edelson.

label: American Abstract Artists
defn: Members of American Abstract Artists, the New York association founded in 1936 to promote abstract art: e.g. Burgoyne Diller, Gertrude Greene, George L. K. Morris, Alice Trumbull Mason.

label: Madhubani Painting
defn: The Mithila painting of women of Bihar and Nepal's Terai, moved from house walls to paper from the 1960s, in bharni, kachni and godna styles: kohbar ghar marriage paintings, Baua Devi nagas.

label: Warli Painting
defn: White rice-paste painting of the Warli of Maharashtra, from marriage chauk on house walls to works on paper (Jivya Soma Mashe): Palaghata chauk, tarpa dance circles.

label: Gond Painting
defn: The painting of the Pardhan Gond of Madhya Pradesh in dot-and-dash infill on paper and canvas since Jangarh Singh Shyam (Jangarh kalam): trees of life, Bhajju Shyam animals.

label: Tanjore Painting
defn: Devotional painting of Thanjavur on wooden board with gesso relief, gold leaf and glass stones, 18th–19th century: Balakrishna, Rama pattabhishekam.

label: Mysore Painting
defn: Devotional painting of the Mysore court in gesso and gold leaf, finer and lighter than Tanjore work: Krishna and Rama icons, Sritattvanidhi illustrations.

label: Truck Art
defn: The painted, mirrored and calligraphic decoration of lorries in Pakistan and India, from Rawalpindi, Peshawar and Karachi workshops: jingle trucks, Horn OK Please tailboards.
aliases: jingle truck;Truck art in South Asia

label: Rickshaw Painting
defn: Hand-painted cycle-rickshaw panels and hoods of Dhaka (UNESCO 2023), with film stars, landscapes and animals: backboard paintings, applique hoods.

label: Letras y Figuras
defn: The 19th-century Philippine genre of watercolour letters composed of figures and scenes, with the costume pictures (tipos del país) of the same Manila painters: name monograms, Damián Domingo costume albums.

label: Ōtsu-e
defn: Folk paintings sold to travellers at Ōtsu on the Tōkaidō from the 17th century, brushed quickly with stencils and few colours: the Demon Chanting the Nembutsu, Wisteria Maiden, Fujimusume, Buddhist icons.

label: Ema
defn: Painted wooden votive plaques offered at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, from small mass-made tablets to large framed ema halls painted by town and ukiyo-e painters: horse ema, Kitano Tenmangū votive tablets.

label: Minhwa
defn: Korean folk painting of the late Joseon period, anonymous decorative screens and scrolls for houses: chaekgeori book-and-scholar's-object screens, munjado ideograph paintings, magpie and tiger, sipjangsaeng ten longevity symbols.

label: Tingatinga Painting
defn: The Dar es Salaam school of enamel painting on board founded by Edward Said Tingatinga in 1968 and carried on by his followers and the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative: flat-coloured animals and birds, crowded village and spirit scenes.

label: Retablo
defn: Small devotional paintings of saints in oil on tin (lámina) made by popular painters in Mexico in the 19th century, with the related ex-voto paintings giving thanks for a miracle: Santo Niño de Atocha láminas, ex-votos of San Juan de los Lagos.

label: Amate Painting
defn: Painting in bright colours on amate bark paper by Nahua artists of the Alto Balsas in Guerrero since the 1960s, with Otomí paper cut-figures from San Pablito: village fiesta scenes, birds and flowers.

label: Tablas de Sarhua
defn: Painted boards of Sarhua (Ayacucho), originally genealogical beams given at house-raisings, later sold as narrative paintings of village life: house-beam tablas, Piraq Causa series.

label: Tigua Painting
defn: Painting on stretched sheepskin by Kichwa artists of Tigua in Ecuador's central highlands, begun by Julio Toaquiza in the 1970s, depicting fiestas and Andean landscapes: Corpus Christi dancers, Cotopaxi landscapes.

label: Fileteado
defn: The decorative painting of Buenos Aires carts, buses and shop signs with scrolls, flowers and lettering, inscribed by UNESCO in 2015: colectivo panels, filete signboards.

label: Bark Painting
defn: Painting in natural ochres on prepared stringybark sheets, the classic medium of Arnhem Land, with clan designs in fine cross-hatching (rarrk) in the east and figurative and x-ray figures in the west: Yolŋu miny'tji clan paintings, Kunwinjku x-ray figures, Groote Eylandt black-ground barks.

label: Theorem Painting
defn: American stencilled still lifes of fruit and flowers painted on velvet or paper with cut stencils (theorems), a schoolgirl and amateur art of c. 1810–1860: fruit baskets on velvet, bowls of flowers.

label: Reverse Glass Painting
defn: Folk pictures painted in reverse on the back of a glass pane, made in glassworks districts of Austria, Bavaria and Bohemia from the 18th century and sold at fairs and shrines: Sandl devotional pictures with the Sandl rose, saints and Madonnas for the home altar.

label: Petrykivka Painting
defn: Ornamental painting of the village of Petrykivka (Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine) with flowers, berries and birds brushed with fingers, cat-hair brushes and reeds on house walls, paper sheets and wooden objects (UNESCO 2013): painted malyovky sheets, painted chests and plates.

label: Tauric Painting
defn: Traditional decorative painting of Mykolaiv Oblast in southern Ukraine, inscribed on the National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Ukraine.

label: Gorodets Painting
defn: Painting of the Gorodets district on the Volga from the mid-19th century, first on distaff bottoms and later on boards, boxes and furniture, with horsemen, ladies, birds and roses in a quick brush style on bright grounds: distaff bottoms (donce), painted panels.

label: Mezen Painting
defn: Red-and-black painting on distaffs, boxes and ladles from the lower Mezen River (Arkhangelsk region), with rows of horses, deer and birds in a graphic, archaic style: Palashchelye distaffs.

label: Northern Dvina Painting
defn: The painting of distaffs, chests and utensils in the villages along the Northern Dvina (Arkhangelsk region), in local styles with red floral grounds, birds, sirins and scenes of sleighing: Borok distaffs, Permogorye distaffs, Rakulka distaffs.

label: Ural-Siberian Painting
defn: Floral painting of the Old Believer and peasant households of the Urals and western Siberia (18th–19th century) on furniture, chests, walls and utensils, with large peonies and roses in a free brush.

label: Zhostovo Painting
defn: Oil painting of flower bouquets on black-lacquered iron trays made in Zhostovo near Moscow since the early 19th century, built up in layers and varnished: bouquet trays, gilded-rim trays.

label: Nizhny Tagil Tray Painting
defn: Painted and lacquered iron trays made in Nizhny Tagil in the Urals from the 18th century, with flowers and genre scenes under a translucent varnish, the forerunner of Zhostovo.

label: Naïve Painting of Kovačica
defn: Naïve painting of the Slovak community of Kovačica in Vojvodina (Serbia) from the 1950s, in oil on canvas and on objects, with village life, harvests and weddings (UNESCO 2024).
aliases: Kovačica naive art;Slovak naive art painting

label: Pysanka
defn: Easter eggs decorated in the Slavic and East European wax-resist (batik) technique with layered dyes and symbolic patterns; regional schools and related types (krashanka, krapanka, drapanka) are kinds: Hutsul pysanky, Boyko pysanky.

label: Haitian Painting
defn: Painting in Haiti since the founding of the Centre d'Art in Port-au-Prince (1944), from the self-taught masters around DeWitt Peters to the Vodou-inspired Saint-Soleil group (1972) and the Jacmel and Cap-Haïtien schools: Hyppolite's Ogoun Ferraille, Philomé Obin's Funeral of Charlemagne Péralte, Big

label: Saz Style
defn: the Ottoman court style of feathery serrated leaves, rosettes and fabulous creatures drawn in ink by the nakkaşhane under Shahkulu and Kara Memi (16th century), and carried from drawings into tiles, textiles and bindings.

label: Ledger Art
defn: Plains narrative drawing in pencil, crayon and ink on the pages of account ledgers and on muslin, from the 1860s, continuing hide painting on paper: the Fort Marion drawings, Cheyenne and Kiowa warrior ledgers, Lakota ledger books.

label: American Comics
defn: Comic strips and comic books of the United States from the newspaper Sunday pages of the 1890s through the superhero comic book, underground comix and the graphic novel: Winsor McCay's Little Nemo in Slumberland, Herriman's Krazy Kat, Kirby and Lee's Fantastic Four, Spiegelman's Maus.
aliases: US comics;American comic books;American comic strips

label: Old Master Drawing
defn: European drawing before c. 1800 as preparatory study and finished work, in metalpoint, chalk, pen and wash: Leonardo's Vitruvian Man, Dürer's Praying Hands, Rembrandt's landscape drawings.

label: Illustration
defn: Drawing made for books, periodicals, posters and caricature from the 18th century to the present: Gillray's caricatures, Tenniel's Alice illustrations, Saul Steinberg's New Yorker covers.

label: Golden Age of Illustration
defn: Book and magazine illustration c. 1880–1920, when colour printing made illustrators celebrities: Arthur Rackham's Peter Pan, Howard Pyle's pirates, Edmund Dulac's Arabian Nights.

label: Ligne Claire
defn: The clear-line drawing style of Hergé and the Brussels school of Franco-Belgian comics: The Adventures of Tintin, Blake and Mortimer.

label: Marcinelle School
defn: The dynamic, rounded Franco-Belgian comics style of Spirou magazine (Jijé, Franquin, Morris): Spirou et Fantasio, Lucky Luke, Gaston.

label: Manga
defn: Japanese comics and their drawn idiom from the 20th century: Tezuka's Astro Boy, Oda's One Piece, Takeuchi's Sailor Moon.

label: Franco-Belgian comics
defn: French-language comics (bande dessinée) of Belgium, France and Switzerland, published as albums: from the Brussels and Marcinelle schools to adult auteur comics and the graphic memoir (Hergé, Franquin, Moebius, Bilal, Satrapi).

label: Đông Hồ Painting
defn: Woodblock prints of Đông Hồ village in Bắc Ninh on điệp (shell-coated) paper with natural colours, sold for Tết: Mouse Wedding, Jealousy, pig and piglets.

label: Hàng Trống Painting
defn: Hanoi's urban folk pictures, printed in outline from woodblocks and hand-coloured: Five Tigers, Carp Gazing at the Moon, Mother Goddess images.

label: Kim Hoàng Painting
defn: Woodblock prints of Kim Hoàng village west of Hanoi, printed on red or yellow paper: Tết pigs and roosters, calligraphic scrolls.

label: Nianhua
defn: Chinese New Year pictures: popular colour woodblock prints of door gods, auspicious children and opera scenes pasted up at the New Year, made in named print towns: Yangliuqing, Taohuawu, Yangjiabu, Zhuxianzhen.
aliases: New Year picture;Chinese New Year prints;nianhua woodblock prints

label: Cordel Literature
defn: The chapbooks of north-eastern Brazil sold hung on strings, whose covers are woodcuts (xilogravura) by popular printmakers: J. Borges woodcuts, cordel covers of Caruaru and Juazeiro.

label: Inuit Printmaking
defn: Stonecut, stencil and lithographic printmaking of Inuit community co-operatives in Canada since 1957, issued in annual collections: Kinngait (Cape Dorset) annual print collections, Baker Lake prints, Kenojuak Ashevak's The Enchanted Owl.

label: Torres Strait Islander Printmaking
defn: The linocut and etching movement of the Torres Strait (Zenadth Kes) from the 1990s, cutting island cosmology, totems and turtle-shell mask forms into large black-and-white prints: Badu and Moa linocuts, Mabuiag etchings.

label: Lubok
defn: Russian popular prints from the 17th to the early 20th century, first woodcuts then copper engravings and lithographs, hand-coloured and sold at fairs, with saints, folk tales, satire and the Mice Burying the Cat: The Mice Burying the Cat, Baba Yaga.

label: Poster Art
defn: The artistic lithographic poster from the colour posters of Jules Chéret in 1870s Paris through the Belle Époque, the Italian, Swiss and British schools and the psychedelic concert poster: Chéret's Bal du Moulin Rouge, Mucha's Gismonda, Toulouse-Lautrec's Divan Japonais, Cappiello's Le Thermogène.

label: Plakatstil
defn: The German 'poster style' founded by Lucian Bernhard's Priester matches poster (1906): a single object, flat colour and a brand name: Bernhard's Priester and Stiller posters, Hohlwein's Riquet, Erdt's Opel, Klinger's Berlin posters.

label: Soviet Poster
defn: The political, film and propaganda poster of Soviet Russia and the USSR from 1917 to 1991, from the Civil War lithographs and ROSTA windows through Constructivist photomontage to the TASS windows and Socialist Realist posters: Moor's Have You Volunteered?, Lissitzky's Beat the Whites with the Red We
aliases: Soviet poster art;Soviet propaganda poster;Russian avant-garde poster

label: Polish School of Posters
defn: The Polish poster art of c. 1950–1990 for film, theatre and circus, painterly, metaphorical and hand-lettered, around Henryk Tomaszewski's Warsaw Academy studio: Tomaszewski's Moore, Lenica's Wozzeck, Cieślewicz's Vertigo, Świerzy's Jimi Hendrix.

label: Old Master Print
defn: Western printmaking before c. 1830 in woodcut, engraving, etching and mezzotint: Dürer's Melencolia I, Rembrandt's Hundred Guilder Print, Piranesi's Carceri.

label: Etching Revival
defn: The re-emergence of etching as an original art c. 1850–1930 in France, Britain and the United States, launched by Cadart's Société des Aquafortistes (1862) and Haden's Royal Society of Painter-Etchers (1880): Whistler's Thames Set, Méryon's Eaux-fortes sur Paris, Seymour Haden's landscapes.

label: Modern Printmaking
defn: Printmaking by artists born c. 1880–1944: the expressionist woodcut, the artist's lithograph and the screenprint: Kollwitz's War cycle, Picasso's Vollard Suite.

label: Contemporary Printmaking
defn: Printmaking by artists born from 1945 across print and multiple practices.

label: Ukiyo-e
defn: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the floating world (17th–19th century): Hokusai's Great Wave, Hiroshige's Fifty-three Stations, Utamaro's beauties.

label: Shin-hanga
defn: The 20th-century Japanese revival of ukiyo-e production by publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō: Kawase Hasui's landscapes, Hashiguchi Goyō's beauties.

label: Sōsaku-hanga
defn: Japanese "creative prints" (from 1904) designed, carved and printed by the artist: Onchi Kōshirō's abstractions, Munakata Shikō's Buddhist prints.

label: Taller de Gráfica Popular
defn: Members of the Taller de Gráfica Popular, the Mexico City printmaking collective founded in 1937 by Leopoldo Méndez, Pablo O'Higgins and Luis Arenal: e.g. Alfredo Zalce, Ángel Bracho, Mariana Yampolsky.

label: Kufic
defn: the angular early Arabic script of Qur'ans on parchment and of inscriptions, with its later Eastern (broken cursive), floriated, plaited and square (banna'i) forms.

label: Maghribi Script
defn: the rounded scripts of al-Andalus, North Africa and West Africa (mabsut, mujawhar, Andalusi, Sudani), written with a pointed pen.

label: Six Pens (al-Aqlam al-Sitta)
defn: the proportioned cursive scripts — thuluth, naskh, muhaqqaq, rayhani, tawqi' and riqa' — codified by Ibn Muqla and Ibn al-Bawwab and perfected by Yaqut al-Musta'simi, then carried by his pupils and by the Ottoman masters (Sheikh Hamdullah, Hafiz Osman).
aliases: aqlam al-sitta; six scripts; Thuluth; Naskh; Muhaqqaq;Islamic calligraphy;Arabic calligraphy

label: Nasta'liq
defn: the hanging Persian script attributed to Mir 'Ali Tabrizi (14th century), the script of Persian poetry and album calligraphy (Sultan 'Ali Mashhadi, Mir 'Ali Haravi, Mir 'Imad), with its shikasta (broken) offshoot.

label: Diwani
defn: the Ottoman chancery script of decrees and imperial documents, with the tughra, the sultan's calligraphic monogram.

label: Sini
defn: Chinese Arabic calligraphy, written with a brush in a rounded style on scrolls and Qur'ans of the Hui Muslims.

label: Mongolian Calligraphy
defn: Writing as an art in the vertical Classical Mongolian script, with its six basic strokes, on paper, silk and wood (UNESCO 2013): sutra manuscripts, calligraphic scrolls.

label: Georgian Calligraphy
defn: Writing of the Georgian scripts (asomtavruli, nuskhuri, mkhedruli) as an art, in manuscripts and inscriptions.

label: Chinese Calligraphy
defn: The art of writing Chinese characters with the brush, in seal, clerical, regular, running and cursive scripts: Wang Xizhi's Lantingji Xu, Huaisu's Autobiography, Mi Fu's Poems Written on a Boat on the Wu River.

label: Japanese Calligraphy
defn: Shodō: the Japanese art of the brush in kanji and kana, with its court lineages (Sesonji-ryū) and Zen bokuseki: Ono no Michikaze's works, Fujiwara no Yukinari's Hakubunshū.

label: Western Calligraphy
defn: The art of Latin-script writing, from Renaissance chancery hands and writing masters to modern lettering: Arrighi's La Operina, Palatino's writing book.

label: Type Design
defn: The design of typefaces and lettering for print and screen since the 19th century: Johnston's Underground typeface, Frutiger's Univers, Miedinger's Helvetica.

label: Korean Calligraphy
defn: seoye: the Korean art of the brush in Hanja and Hangul, from Silla and Goryeo masters to the Joseon court and the Chusa style of Kim Jeong-hui: Kim Saeng's works, Han Ho's Seokbong style, Kim Jeong-hui's Chusa-che.

label: Early Qur'anic Manuscripts
defn: Qur'ans written on parchment in Hijazi and Kufic scripts from the 7th to the 10th century, in horizontal format with sparse illuminated headings (the Blue Qur'an, the Tübingen and Birmingham fragments).
aliases: early Qur'ans; Hijazi Qur'ans; Kufic Qur'ans

label: Islamic Illumination
defn: the illumination of Qur'ans and books after about 1000: gilded and painted frontispieces, sura headings, margins and borders, in the Abbasid, Mamluk, Ilkhanid, Timurid and Safavid (tazhib), Ottoman (tezhip) and Mughal traditions, with its named illuminators.

label: Timbuktu Manuscripts
defn: the manuscripts of the West African Islamic scholarly tradition (Timbuktu, Djenné, the Sahel), in Arabic and in Ajami (African languages in Arabic script), with their Sudani script and leather satchel bindings.

label: Malay Manuscripts
defn: illuminated Malay manuscripts in Jawi script from the Islamic sultanates of the Malay world (Aceh, Terengganu, Java), with their floral frontispieces.

label: Palm-Leaf Manuscripts
defn: Books of incised or inked palm leaves strung between wooden boards, the manuscript tradition of South Asia and Sri Lanka: Tamil and Grantha olas, Odia incised and painted pothis, Sinhalese Pali texts, Pala Buddhist Prajnaparamita.

label: Lontar
defn: Manuscripts on incised leaves of the lontar palm, blackened with soot, the book form of Bali, Lombok and older Java: Kakawin Sutasoma, Nagarakretagama, illustrated prasi leaves.

label: Folding-Book Manuscripts
defn: Concertina-folded books of mulberry or khoi paper, lacquered at the ends, in Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia: parabaik, samut khoi, Lanna phap sa, kraing.
aliases: folding book manuscript;parabaik;samut khoi;samut thai;kraing;phap sa

label: Kammavaca
defn: Burmese ordination texts written in square tamarind-seed script in lacquer and gold on lacquered palm leaf, cloth or metal: gilt kammavaca leaves, painted covers.

label: Pustaha
defn: The divination and ritual books of the Batak datu, written on folded tree bark between carved wooden covers: Great Pustaha.

label: Dunhuang Manuscripts
defn: The manuscripts sealed in the Library Cave (Cave 17) of the Mogao Caves about 1000 and opened in 1900: Buddhist sutras, documents and the earliest dated printed book, the Diamond Sutra of 868, with illustrated sutra frontispieces.

label: Uigwe
defn: Illustrated royal protocol books of the Joseon court (1392–1910), recording ceremonies, weddings and funerals in text and painted processions: Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe, Banchado procession paintings.

label: Sutra Copying
defn: Buddhist sutras transcribed as acts of devotion and decorated with gold and silver on dyed paper, frontispiece paintings and ornamented rollers in Japan and Korea: the Heike Nōkyō, Lotus Sutra fan papers, Goryeo sagyeong in gold on indigo paper.

label: Dongba Manuscripts
defn: Ritual manuscripts of the Naxi Dongba priests of Lijiang in Yunnan, written in pictographic Dongba script and painted with deities, with painted ritual cards and scrolls.

label: Ethiopian Manuscripts
defn: The Ge'ez (and later Amharic) manuscript tradition of the Ethiopian and Eritrean church: parchment codices in wooden boards with blind-tooled leather, written in Ge'ez script with ornamental harag frames: gospel books, Psalters, Arganonä Maryam prayer books.

label: Book of the Dead
defn: Illustrated Egyptian funerary papyri of spells for the afterlife, with painted vignettes, New Kingdom to Ptolemaic: Papyrus of Ani, Papyrus of Hunefer, Greenfield Papyrus.
aliases: Egyptian funerary papyri;Coming Forth by Day

label: Maya Codices
defn: The surviving bark-paper screenfold books of the Postclassic Maya, written in hieroglyphs with painted almanacs: Dresden Codex, Madrid Codex, Paris Codex, Maya Codex of Mexico.

label: Late Antique Illumination
defn: Illustrated and decorated Latin books of late antiquity, 4th–7th century, in rustic capitals and uncial: Vergilius Vaticanus, St Augustine Gospels, Codex Argenteus.

label: Insular Illumination
defn: Manuscript art of Ireland and Britain, c. 600–900, joining Celtic, Germanic and Mediterranean ornament in carpet pages and great initials: Book of Durrow, Lindisfarne Gospels, Book of Kells, Book of Armagh.

label: Merovingian Illumination
defn: Book decoration of Frankish Gaul, 7th–8th century, with zoomorphic initials of fish and birds: Gellone Sacramentary, Gelasian Sacramentary.

label: Carolingian Illumination
defn: Manuscript painting of the Frankish empire, c. 780–900, in its court and monastic schools: Godescalc Evangelistary, Coronation Gospels, Utrecht Psalter, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram.

label: Ottonian Illumination
defn: Manuscript painting of the Ottonian empire, c. 950–1050, at Reichenau, Trier, Echternach, Cologne and Regensburg: Gospels of Otto III, Pericopes of Henry II, Registrum Gregorii, Bamberg Apocalypse.

label: Anglo-Saxon Illumination
defn: Late Anglo-Saxon manuscript art, 10th–11th century, in the acanthus-bordered Winchester style and in outline drawing: Benedictional of St Æthelwold, Harley Psalter, Ramsey Psalter.

label: Mozarabic Illumination
defn: Manuscript painting of early medieval Christian Iberia, 10th–11th century, in flat banded colour, above all the illustrated commentaries of Beatus of Liébana: Morgan Beatus, Gerona Beatus, León Bible of 960.
aliases: Spanish illumination of the Early Middle Ages;Visigothic illumination

label: Romanesque Illumination
defn: Manuscript painting of Latin Europe c. 1050–1200, with large-format Bibles and monumental figure style: Bury Bible, Winchester Bible, St Albans Psalter, Hortus deliciarum.

label: Renaissance Illumination
defn: Manuscript illumination of the 15th–16th century influenced by Renaissance painting, in Italy, France and the courts that collected it: Farnese Hours, Bible of Borso d'Este, Hours of Étienne Chevalier, Corvinian manuscripts.

label: Hebrew Illuminated Manuscripts
defn: Decorated and illustrated Hebrew books of the Middle Ages and early modern period — Bibles, haggadot and mahzorim — with micrography and painted cycles: Sarajevo Haggadah, Golden Haggadah, Birds' Head Haggadah, Rothschild Miscellany.

label: Russian Illuminated Manuscripts
defn: Gospel books, chronicles and service books of Kievan Rus' and Muscovy, 11th–17th century, with Byzantine-derived miniatures and teratological headpieces and initials: Ostromir Gospels, Khitrovo Gospels, Radziwiłł Chronicle.

label: Fraktur
defn: Illuminated folk documents of the Pennsylvania Germans, 18th–19th century, lettered in a broken script and painted with birds, hearts and tulips: Taufschein (birth and baptismal certificates), Vorschrift (writing samples).

label: Gothic Book Illustration
defn: The illumination of Gothic manuscripts (13th–15th century), from Paris workshops to the Books of Hours: Jean Pucelle's Hours of Jeanne d'Évreux, the Douce Apocalypse, the Bedford Hours.

label: Ghent-Bruges School
defn: Flemish manuscript illumination c. 1475–1560 with illusionistic borders: the Grimani Breviary, Simon Bening's Da Costa Hours.

label: Islamic Bookbinding
defn: the bindings of the Islamic book: tooled, stamped and filigree-cut leather with the envelope flap, and from the 15th century painted lacquer bindings.

label: Treasure Binding
defn: Medieval European book covers worked by goldsmiths in gold, silver-gilt, enamel, gems and carved ivory for Gospel books and altar books, c. 700–1200: Lindau Gospels upper cover, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram, Ashburnham Pentateuch ivory covers, Gospels of Theodelinda.
aliases: jewelled binding;jeweled book cover;cover of a Gospel book

label: Fine Binding
defn: Decorated leather bookbinding of Europe and America from the Gothic blind-stamped binding through Renaissance gold tooling to the designer bindings of the 20th century, named after binders, patrons and tooling styles: Grolier bindings, à la fanfare, Le Gascon pointillé, Derome dentelle, Cobden-Sande
aliases: European fine binding;fine bindings;decorated bookbinding;gold-tooled binding

label: East Asian Bookbinding
defn: the book forms of China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam, from scrolls, concertina and butterfly bindings to side-stitched thread binding (xianzhuang) of folded leaves in cloth cases: Ming and Qing xianzhuang books, Japanese fukuro-toji wahon, Korean five-hole bindings.
aliases: xianzhuang; thread binding; stab binding; fukuro-toji

label: Ebru
defn: paper marbling as practised in Ottoman Turkey and Iran: colours floated on size and transferred to paper, used for album margins and endpapers.

label: Sanjhi
defn: Paper-stencil cutting of the Braj temples of Mathura and Vrindavan, used to lay coloured powder images: Krishna lila stencils.

label: Chinese Paper Cutting
defn: Designs cut from red and coloured paper with scissors or knives for windows, doors and festivals across China (UNESCO 2009): window flowers (chuanghua), xi double-happiness cuts, embroidery patterns.

label: Papel Picado
defn: Mexican cut tissue paper banners chiselled through stacked sheets with designs for the Day of the Dead and fiestas.

label: Vytsinanka
defn: Belarusian folk paper cutting, symmetrical designs cut with scissors from folded paper for interiors and festivals (UNESCO 2024).

label: Slovenian Paper Flower Making
defn: The Slovenian craft of making crepe and tissue paper flowers for church feasts, processions and festive decoration.

label: Oil-Paper Umbrella
defn: the craft of bamboo-ribbed umbrellas covered in hand-made paper, waterproofed with tung or persimmon oil and painted with flowers, birds and calligraphy, from China to Japan and Southeast Asia: Luzhou and Meinong oil-paper umbrellas, Japanese wagasa, Pathein umbrellas.

label: Fan Making
defn: the making and painting of hand fans, folding and flat, in paper, silk, bamboo, ivory and lacquer, studied as decorated objects with named centres: Kyoto sensu and uchiwa, Hangzhou folding fans, Valencian painted fans, Parisian éventails.
aliases: éventail; hand fan; sensu; uchiwa; shanzi

label: Chōchin
defn: the Japanese craft of collapsible paper lanterns of washi stretched over a spiral split-bamboo frame, painted or lettered with crests and scenes, in named centres: Gifu chōchin, Odawara chōchin, Mito chōchin.

label: Scherenschnitte
defn: the scissor-cut paper silhouettes and pictures of German-speaking Switzerland and Germany, carried by Pennsylvania Germans to America in the 18th century: Pays-d'Enhaut alpine cuts, Johann Jakob Hauswirth, Pennsylvania German love letters.

label: Kirie
defn: Japanese paper-cut pictures, cut with a knife from black or coloured paper, often backed with colour, from Edo katagami practice to modern kirie artists.

label: Wycinanki
defn: Polish folk paper cutting in bright layered colours, made for cottage walls and festivals in named regional styles: Łowicz layered cuts, Kurpie single-colour leluje.

label: Hanji
defn: Korean handmade paper of paper-mulberry bark formed on the we bal mould and pounded (dochim) since the Goryeo period, and the crafts made of it: jiseung paper-cord weaving, jeonji coloured-paper boxes.

label: Samarra Stucco
defn: the carved and moulded stucco of the Abbasid capital Samarra (9th century) in its three styles, of which the third, the bevelled style, carried abstract ornament across the early Islamic world.

label: Nasrid Stucco (Yesería)
defn: the carved and painted stucco of Nasrid Granada and the Mudéjar workshops (Alhambra wall panels, muqarnas).

label: Assyrian Palace Reliefs
defn: Carved gypsum (Mosul alabaster) orthostat reliefs from Neo-Assyrian palaces, 9th–7th century BC, with lamassu gateway figures: Ashurnasirpal II at Nimrud, Sennacherib's Lachish reliefs, Ashurbanipal's lion hunt at Nineveh.

label: Andalusian Ivories
defn: carved ivory boxes and pyxides of the Umayyad caliphal workshops of Córdoba and Madinat al-Zahra and of the taifa courts (10th–11th century).

label: Siculo-Arabic Ivories
defn: painted and gilded ivory caskets made in Norman Sicily and southern Italy (12th–13th century) in an Arabic decorative idiom.

label: Begram Ivories
defn: Carved ivory and bone plaques and furniture fittings of the 1st–2nd century found in the Kushan treasure at Begram (Kapisa) in Afghanistan, in an Indian idiom: river-goddess brackets, openwork throne-leg panels.

label: Netsuke
defn: Miniature toggles carved in ivory, wood and other materials to secure hanging containers to the kimono sash, Edo to Meiji period, with named carvers and regional schools: katabori figures, manjū netsuke, sashi netsuke.

label: Benin Ivories
defn: Ivory carved for the Oba of Benin by the Igbesanmwan guild and in neighbouring Owo, 15th–19th century: pendant masks of the Iyoba Idia, carved tusks for royal altars, double gongs and armlets.

label: Afro-Portuguese Ivories
defn: Ivories carved by Sapi (Sierra Leone), Edo (Benin) and Kongo carvers for Portuguese patrons in the 15th–16th century: salt cellars, side-blown oliphants, spoons and pyxes.

label: Nimrud Ivories
defn: Carved, gilded and inlaid ivory plaques and figures of the 9th–7th century BC found at the Assyrian capital Nimrud, made in Assyrian, Phoenician and North Syrian styles: Lioness attacking a Nubian, Woman at the Window, furniture plaques.

label: Byzantine Ivories
defn: Ivory carving of the Byzantine empire, 5th–12th century: consular diptychs, Barberini Ivory, Romanos group icons, Veroli Casket.

label: Alaska Native Ivory Carving
defn: Carving and engraving of walrus ivory and bone by the Iñupiat, Yupik and St Lawrence Island peoples of the Bering Strait, from ancient engraved hunting gear to figures, cribbage boards and engraved tusks for the curio trade.
aliases: walrus ivory carving;Bering Strait ivory carving;Eskimo ivory

label: Mississippian Shell Gorgets
defn: Engraved discs of marine-shell worn at the neck in the Mississippian Southeast (c. 1000–1600), cut with Southeastern Ceremonial Complex imagery: Spiro and Etowah gorgets, rattlesnake and cross-in-circle gorgets, mask gorgets.

label: Gothic Ivories
defn: Elephant-ivory carving of Gothic Europe, c. 1200–1530, led by Parisian workshops: devotional diptychs and polyptychs, statuettes of the Virgin, mirror cases and caskets with romance scenes.

label: Scrimshaw
defn: Engraving and carving on whale teeth, whalebone and walrus ivory by sailors of the whaling fleets, 18th–19th century: engraved sperm-whale teeth, busks, jagging wheels.

label: Duodji
defn: The handicraft of the Sámi of Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola peninsula, divided into hard duodji (antler, bone and wood) and soft duodji (leather, textiles and pewter-thread embroidery): antler-handled knives, carved drinking cups (guksi), pewter-thread embroidered bags.

label: Uelen Bone Carving
defn: Engraving and carving of walrus ivory by Chukchi and Yupik carvers at Uelen in Chukotka, institutionalised as a workshop in 1931: engraved walrus tusks with hunting scenes, small figures of walrus and bears.

label: Tobolsk Bone Carving
defn: Bone and mammoth-ivory carving of Tobolsk in western Siberia from the 18th century, with small sculptures of northern life (reindeer sleds, hunters); a factory since 1929.

label: Yakut Bone Carving
defn: Mammoth-ivory carving of the Sakha (Yakutia), from 19th-century combs and caskets to Soviet-era sculptural compositions combined with silver and leather.

label: Torre del Greco Shell and Coral Carving
defn: the carving of shell cameos and Mediterranean coral at Torre del Greco near Naples from the 17th century, cut with the bulino scraper: sardonyx-shell cameo brooches, carved coral branches and beads.
aliases: Torre del Greco cameos; shell cameo carving; Neapolitan coral carving

label: Romanesque Ivories
defn: walrus-ivory, whalebone and elephant-ivory carving of northern Europe, 11th-12th century, from English and Scandinavian (Trondheim) workshops: Lewis chessmen, Bury St Edmunds Cross, Gloucester Candlestick.
aliases: Romanesque ivory carving; Norse walrus-ivory carving

label: Fatimid Rock Crystal
defn: vessels and objects carved from rock crystal in Fatimid Egypt (10th–11th century), above all the ewers with relief decoration later mounted in European church treasuries.

label: Mughal Jade
