defn: the lamp-blown and mould-blown glass of Lauscha in Thuringia (from the 16th century), silvered inside and hand-painted, where the glass Christmas bauble originated and was exported worldwide from the 1840s: blown baubles, figural ornaments, glass eyes and marbles.
aliases: Lauschaer Glas; Lauscha glass ornaments; Thuringian glass Christmas ornaments

label: Edo Glass
defn: the hand-blown and lampworked glass of Tokyo from the late Edo period, a designated traditional craft (Edo garasu): inside-painted Edo fūrin wind bells, Sasaki-type glass pens.
aliases: Edo garasu; Edo fūrin; Tokyo glass

label: Roman Micromosaic
defn: pictures and jewellery made of minute pulled-glass (smalti filati) tesserae in Rome from the late 18th century, led by the Vatican Mosaic Studio and sold on the Grand Tour: micromosaic plaques of Roman views, snuff-box lids, brooches.

label: Egyptian Hand-Blown Glass
defn: the free-blown glass of Cairo's workshops, including recycled Muski glass and the decorative bottles of the Khan el-Khalili perfume trade: perfume-oil bottles, Muski tumblers.

label: Islamic Cut Glass
defn: glass decorated by wheel-cutting and relief-carving in Iran, Iraq and Egypt (9th–11th century), from facet-cut bowls to relief-cut cameo glass and the Hedwig glasses.

label: Bohemian Glass
defn: Glass of Bohemia from the late 17th century, potash-lime crystal decorated by wheel-engraving and cutting, later with coloured and cased glass: engraved goblets, Zwischengoldglas, Biedermeier cased glass.

label: Edo Kiriko
defn: the cut glass of Tokyo founded by Kagaya Kyūbei in 1834, clear or colour-cased glass wheel-cut in fine geometric patterns (yarai, kiku-tsunagi, nanako): cased sake cups, cut tumblers.

label: Mamluk Enamelled Glass
defn: enamelled and gilded glass of Ayyubid and Mamluk Syria and Egypt (13th–14th century): mosque lamps, beakers and bottles with blazons and inscriptions.

label: Islamic Lustre-Painted Glass
defn: glass stained with metallic lustre in Egypt, Syria and Iraq (8th–11th century), the predecessor of lustre pottery.

label: Medieval Stained Glass
defn: Coloured pot-metal glass painted with vitreous paint (and from c. 1300 silver stain) and leaded into windows for the churches of Latin Europe, c. 1100-1500, from Romanesque and High Gothic cathedral glazing to late Gothic workshops: Chartres and Sainte-Chapelle windows, Canterbury Miracle windows, E

label: Painted Glass Roundels
defn: Small panes of colourless glass painted in vitreous paint and silver stain, set into domestic and cloister windows in the Low Countries, northern France and the Rhineland, c. 1480-1560, often after designs by painters: roundels from the circle of the Master of the Amsterdam Cabinet, Labours of the M

label: Tiffany Glass
defn: The opalescent and iridescent glass of Louis Comfort Tiffany's studios in New York (1878-1933) and the American opalescent window movement he shared with John La Farge: leaded windows, lamps, mosaics and blown Favrile vessels: Tiffany Studios wisteria lamps, Favrile vases, La Farge's Peonies Blown i
aliases: American opalescent glass;opalescent stained glass;Favrile glass

label: Khurasan Metalwork
defn: cast and inlaid brass of eastern Iran and Herat (12th–13th century), with silver and copper inlay and figural bands (the Bobrinsky Bucket, 1163).

label: Mosul School of Metalwork
defn: inlaid brass made by craftsmen with the nisba al-Mawsili in Mosul, Syria and Egypt (13th century), the model for Ayyubid and Mamluk inlay.

label: Mamluk Metalwork
defn: inlaid brass and bronze of Mamluk Egypt and Syria (1250–1517) — basins, candlesticks, Qur'an boxes — with epigraphic blazons (the Baptistère de Saint Louis by Muhammad ibn al-Zayn).

label: Veneto-Saracenic Metalwork
defn: inlaid brass made in the Islamic manner in the 15th–16th century and long thought Venetian, now mostly given to Mamluk and Iranian workshops.

label: Ottoman Tombak
defn: fire-gilded copper of the Ottoman court (17th–19th century): ewers, basins, censers and mosque fittings.

label: Bidri Ware
defn: zinc-alloy objects inlaid with silver and blackened, from Bidar in the Deccan (from the 14th century).

label: Koftgari
defn: damascening of steel with gold and silver wire, practised in Mughal and Rajput India and in Iran for arms and objects.

label: Islamic Astrolabes
defn: brass astrolabes and celestial globes of the Islamic world, engraved instruments made by named makers in Baghdad, Isfahan, Lahore and al-Andalus.

label: Firoozeh Koobi
defn: Iranian metal objects set with turquoise chips in a mosaic over the surface (Isfahan, Mashhad).

label: Persian Metalwork
defn: inlaid and engraved brass and steel of Iran after the Mongols: Inju Fars inlay (14th century), Timurid and Safavid tinned-brass jugs, candlesticks and inkwells with poetic inscriptions, and Qajar cut steel (Hajji 'Abbas).
aliases: Timurid metalwork; Safavid metalwork; Qajar steel

label: Sogdian Silver
defn: Chased, engraved and gilded silver vessels of the Sogdian city-states (6th–9th century), many found in the Urals and Siberia: cups with roundels of ibexes, bowls with banquet and hunting scenes.

label: Animal Style
defn: The art of the Eurasian steppe nomads (Scythian, Saka, Sarmatian, Ordos, Xiongnu), 9th century BCE–3rd century CE, in which stylised and contorted animals cover gold and bronze plaques, harness and weapons: curled-feline plaques, Arzhan deer, Ordos belt buckles.

label: Dong Son Drums
defn: Bronze kettle drums of the Đông Sơn culture of northern Vietnam (c. 500 BCE–300 CE), cast with star-centred tympana, frogs and processions, traded across the archipelago: Ngọc Lũ drum, Hoàng Hạ drum, Makalamau of Sangeang.
aliases: Đông Sơn drums;Heger type I drums

label: Burmese Silver
defn: Repoussé and chased silver of Burma, 19th–early 20th century, with crowded narrative and zodiac friezes: offering bowls, betel boxes, presentation cups.

label: Chinese Ritual Bronzes
defn: Bronze vessels and bells cast in piece-moulds for ancestral rites from the Erligang and Shang to the Han: ding cauldrons, gu and jue wine vessels, taotie masks, inscribed Western Zhou gui.

label: Ordos Bronzes
defn: Cast bronze belt plaques, knives and fittings in the steppe animal style from the Ordos and northern frontier of China (6th–1st century BCE).

label: Yugi
defn: Korean bronze tableware forged or cast from high-tin bronze (bangjja yugi), of Anseong and Napcheong; makers designated yugijang.

label: Ipsa
defn: Korean inlay of silver and gold wire into iron and bronze (Goryeo to Joseon): incense burners, kundika and furniture fittings; makers designated ipsajang.

label: Ethiopian Crosses
defn: Processional, hand and pectoral crosses of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in cast brass, silver and carved wood, with openwork lattices: Lalibela processional crosses, Gondar crosses, hand crosses.

label: Akan Goldweights
defn: Small brass weights cast by lost wax by the Akan for weighing gold dust, geometric and figurative (proverbs): abrammuo, with kuduo vessels and forowa boxes of the same casters.

label: Igbo-Ukwu Bronzes
defn: Leaded-bronze vessels and regalia cast by lost wax at Igbo-Ukwu (9th–10th century), with dense granular surfaces: roped pot, shell-shaped bowl, pendant ornaments.

label: Luristan Bronzes
defn: Cast bronze horse-bits, finials, standards, pins and weapons from the Zagros mountains of western Iran, early 1st millennium BC: master-of-animals finials, cheekpieces with winged creatures, votive pins.

label: Achaemenid Metalwork
defn: Gold and silver vessels and ornaments of the Persian empire, 6th–4th century BC: gold fluted bowls and rhyta, Oxus Treasure, griffin-handled amphorae.

label: Sasanian Silver
defn: Silver and silver-gilt vessels of Sasanian Iran, 3rd–7th century, hammered and chased with royal hunts and Dionysiac scenes: royal hunting plates, ewers with dancing figures, high-footed bowls.

label: Etruscan Mirrors
defn: Bronze hand mirrors of Etruria and Latium with mythological scenes engraved on the back, 6th–2nd century BC, together with the engraved cistae of Praeneste: mirror with Minerva and Hercules, Ficoroni Cista.

label: Moche Metalwork
defn: Gold, silver and gilded-copper objects of the Moche, worked by depletion gilding and inlaid with turquoise and shell: Sipán ear ornaments, backflaps, nose ornaments.

label: Sicán Metalwork
defn: Gold and tumbaga objects of the Sicán (Lambayeque) culture of Peru's north coast (c. 900–1100 CE): Sicán funerary masks, tumi knives, beakers.

label: Chimú Metalwork
defn: Hammered and repoussé silver and gold of the Chimú kingdom (c. 900–1470 CE): beakers, ear spools, feathered tunics with plaques.

label: Inca Metalwork
defn: Gold and silver of the Inca empire (c. 1400–1532): cast and hammered figurines from capacocha offerings, keros and ornaments: silver llamas, gold female figurines.

label: Muisca Goldwork
defn: Lost-wax tumbaga castings of the Muisca of the Colombian highlands (c. 600–1600 CE), above all the votive tunjos: Muisca raft, tunjo figures.

label: Colonial Andean Silverwork
defn: The silver of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) from Potosí, Cusco and Lima: church plate, sahumadores, and the domestic and equestrian silver that continued in the Río de la Plata: incense burners in animal form, mate cups, altar frontals.

label: La Tène Art
defn: The curvilinear art of the Iron Age Celts, c. 450 BC to the Roman conquest, chiefly in bronze and gold metalwork: Basse-Yutz flagons, Waldalgesheim style torcs, Battersea Shield.

label: Migration Period Art
defn: The metalwork of the Germanic peoples, c. 300–800, in polychrome garnet cloisonné and the interlaced animal styles I and II: brooches and fibulae, Lombard gold-foil crosses, Visigothic votive crowns of Guarrazar.

label: Anglo-Saxon Metalwork
defn: Metalwork of Anglo-Saxon England, 5th–11th century, from garnet-cloisonné and filigree gold to Trewhiddle-style silver: Sutton Hoo great buckle, Staffordshire Hoard, Fuller Brooch.

label: Viking Art
defn: The animal-ornament art of Scandinavia and its settlements, c. 750–1100, in its succession of styles named after finds (Oseberg, Borre, Jelling, Mammen, Ringerike, Urnes), chiefly in metal and wood: Oseberg ship carvings, Mammen axe, Urnes stave church portal.

label: South Staffordshire Enamels
defn: English painted enamel on copper of c. 1750–1800 from Bilston, Wednesbury, Birmingham and London (popularly 'Battersea enamels'): snuffboxes, étuis, patch boxes, cassolettes.

label: Ormolu
defn: Fire-gilt bronze of 17th–19th-century France and its imitators, cast and chased for furniture mounts, clocks and candelabra, and for mounting Chinese and Japanese porcelain: mounted porcelain vases, Gouthière candelabra.

label: Kubachi Silver
defn: Silver and metalwork of the Dargin village of Kubachi in Dagestan: engraved, niello and filigree vessels, arms and jewellery with dense floral ornament.

label: Kasli Iron Casting
defn: Cast-iron sculpture and openwork made at the Kasli works in the Urals since the 19th century: Kasli cast-iron pavilion (Paris 1900), statuettes of horsemen and animals.

label: Finift
defn: Painted enamel on copper of Russia, above all of Rostov the Great from the 18th century: icons, medallions and jewellery painted in enamel colours.

label: Hutsul Metalwork
defn: The brass casting and metal inlay of the Hutsuls of the Carpathians: cast crosses, jewellery, pipes and toporets axes, and brass-inlaid wood (UNESCO-listed in the Ukrainian National Inventory).
aliases: metalworking traditions of the Hutsul region

label: Drotárstvo
defn: Slovak wire craft developed by itinerant tinkers who mended pottery with wire and later made wire objects and sculpture (UNESCO 2023).

label: Limoges Enamel
defn: Enamel on copper made at Limoges, first as gilt champlevé (Œuvre de Limoges, c. 1150-1350) for reliquaries and liturgical objects, then as painted enamel and grisaille (c. 1470-1630) by dynasties of enamellers: champlevé chasses of Thomas Becket, Pénicaud triptychs, Léonard Limosin portraits, Pierre
aliases: Œuvre de Limoges;opus lemovicense;Limoges painted enamel;émail de Limoges

label: Augsburg Goldsmiths' Work
defn: The silver and gold of the guild goldsmiths of the imperial city of Augsburg, Europe's leading exporter of display plate from the late 16th to the 18th century: embossed repoussé dishes and ewers, silver-gilt toilet services, Hildesheim prince-bishop's service, enamel- and gem-mounted Baroque cabine

label: English Silver
defn: Domestic, ceremonial and church plate made by the goldsmiths of London and the English assay towns from the Tudor period to the 19th century, transformed after 1685 by Huguenot refugee silversmiths: Huguenot ewers and wine cisterns, Paul de Lamerie's Rococo tea kettles, Georgian tea services, Regenc

label: Byzantine Enamel
defn: Gold cloisonné enamel of the Byzantine empire, 6th–12th century, in full (Vollschmelz) and sunk (Senkschmelz) techniques, on reliquaries, icons, crowns and book covers: Limburg Staurotheke, Pala d'Oro plaques, Holy Crown of Hungary, Fieschi Morgan Staurotheke.

label: Chinese Cloisonné
defn: Cloisonné enamel on copper and bronze made in China from the early Ming (dated pieces from the Xuande reign, 1426–35) and at its height in the Qing imperial workshops, its turquoise grounds giving the name jingtailan: Xuande-mark lotus jars, Jingtai-mark gu vases, Qianlong cloisonné altar sets and e

label: Japanese Cloisonné
defn: Japanese cloisonné enamel (shippō), revived by Kaji Tsunekichi of Owari in the 1830s and brought to its golden age c. 1880–1910 by the Kyoto and Tokyo workshops, with wired (yūsen) and wireless (musen) pictorial enamels: Namikawa Yasuyuki's Kyoto vases, Namikawa Sōsuke's Akasaka Palace medallions, A

label: Mosan Art
defn: Romanesque goldsmiths' work and enamel of the Meuse valley (11th–13th century): Nicholas of Verdun's Klosterneuburg Altar, the Stavelot Triptych.

label: Jura Watchmaking
defn: mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics (automata, music boxes) of the Franco-Swiss Jura arc and Geneva, 17th century to the present, with engraved and gilt movements, enamelled cases and painted dials; inscribed by UNESCO in 2020: Geneva enamel watches, Jura complications, automata.
aliases: Swiss watchmaking; Geneva watchmaking; craftsmanship of mechanical watchmaking and art mechanics

label: Black Forest Clockmaking
defn: cottage and factory clocks of Triberg and Furtwangen, mid-17th c.–present, with painted shield dials and carved cuckoo-clock cases.
aliases: Black Forest clocks; cuckoo clocks; Schwarzwälder Uhren

label: London Clockmaking
defn: london clocks of c. 1660–1800 (Knibb, Tompion, Quare): ebony and marquetry longcase and bracket clocks, engraved backplates.
aliases: English clockmaking (London school); London longcase clocks

label: Glashütte Watchmaking
defn: saxon watchmaking of Glashütte from A. Lange's 1845 workshop, with three-quarter plates and hand-engraved balance cocks.

label: Comtoise Clockmaking
defn: provincial French longcase clocks of Franche-Comté (Morbier, Morez), 1680–c. 1910, with embossed brass lyre pendulums and painted cases.

label: Mora Clockmaking
defn: swedish longcase clocks of Mora in Dalarna, late 18th–19th c., cottage movements in painted, waisted pine cases.

label: Wadokei
defn: japanese clocks of the Edo period showing unequal temporal hours: pillar, pillow and bracket clocks in lacquered and engraved cases.

label: Vienna Regulator Clockmaking
defn: weight-driven precision wall clocks of Vienna, c. 1780–1930, in glazed Biedermeier and later historicist cases.

label: Connecticut Clockmaking
defn: mass-produced shelf clocks of Connecticut from Eli Terry (c. 1814): pillar-and-scroll and OG cases with reverse-painted glass tablets.

label: Moroccan Metalwork
defn: the brass and copper work of Fez, Marrakesh and Meknes, pierced, chased and worked in repoussé with geometric and floral openwork: pierced lanterns set with coloured glass, trays, incense burners.

label: Nanbu Tekki
defn: cast iron of the old Nanbu domain (Morioka and Mizusawa, Iwate) from the 17th century, sand-cast with arare hailstone and relief patterns: tetsubin kettles, chagama tea kettles, furin wind bells.
aliases: Nambu ironware; Nanbu ironware; Nambu tekki

label: Solingen Cutlery
defn: blades of the Klingenstadt Solingen, medieval–present: etched sword blades, then knives, scissors and razors.

label: Thiers Cutlery
defn: cutlery of Thiers on the Durolle, documented from the 13th c., France's main knife centre (Sabatier, Laguiole makers).

label: Uchihamono
defn: Japanese forged blades, steel forge-welded to soft iron, clay-quenched and hand-sharpened, made in centres designated as traditional crafts: Sakai, Echizen, Tosa, Banshu Miki and Echigo Sanjo uchihamono.
aliases: Japanese forged blades; hamono; Japanese cutlery

label: Sheffield Cutlery
defn: cutlery of Sheffield under the Cutlers' Company of Hallamshire (1624), with crucible steel (1740s) and pearl and ivory handles.

label: European Scientific Instruments
defn: mathematical, optical and philosophical instruments of Europe from the Renaissance to the 19th century, of engraved and lacquered brass in veneered cases, made by named workshops: Latin astrolabes, London telescopes and microscopes, wheel barometers.
aliases: scientific instruments; mathematical instruments; philosophical instruments

label: Nachiarkoil Lamps
defn: hollow-cast brass lamps made since 1857 by Kammalar families at Nachiarkoil in Tamil Nadu in river-sand moulds (GI 2010): kuthuvilakku standing lamps, annam swan lamps.

label: Western Silversmithing
defn: the hand-engraved silver of the American West since the 1920s, with overlay figures and gold trim on belt buckles, spurs, bits and conchos, above all rodeo trophy buckles.
aliases: Western silver; cowboy silver; trophy buckles

label: Islamic Arms and Armour
defn: the arms and armour of the Islamic courts: Mamluk and Ottoman helmets and mail, Persian shamshirs and watered-steel (wootz) blades, Ottoman yatağans and Mughal talwars, katars and jade-hilted daggers.
aliases: shamshir; yatağan; talwar; wootz steel; Damascus steel

label: Kris
defn: The asymmetrical pattern-welded (pamor) dagger of Java and the Malay world (UNESCO 2005), with carved hilts and sheaths, in regional forms from Sumatra to Mindanao: Javanese keris with naga blade, Balinese figural hilts, Bugis sheaths, Moro kalis.

label: Japanese Swords
defn: Blades forged and polished by Japanese swordsmiths in named traditions and schools: tachi, katana, tantō of the five traditions (Yamashiro, Yamato, Bizen, Sōshū, Mino).

label: Japanese Sword Mountings
defn: Metal sword fittings (tosogu) made by schools of metalworkers from the Muromachi to the Meiji: tsuba guards, menuki, kozuka, fuchi-kashira, in shakudō, shibuichi and mokume-gane.

label: Milanese Armour
defn: Plate armour of Milan, the leading European centre from c. 1400 to the 16th century (the Missaglia and Negroli families), from smooth white harness to embossed parade armour all'antica: Avant armour, Negroli burgonets.

label: Puukko
defn: The traditional Finnish belt knife with a wooden or birch-bark handle and leather sheath, made by named smiths (Kauhava, Fiskars).

label: Longquan Swords
defn: swords forged at Longquan in Zhejiang, by tradition from the smith Ou Yezi, with folded steel and fittings in brass and rayskin (national ICH 2006): jian, dao.

label: Khukuri
defn: the forward-curving chopping knife of Nepal, forged with fullers and carried in sheaths with chased silver chapes, the weapon of the Gurkhas: Ang Khola, Dui Chira, ceremonial silver-mounted khukuris.

label: Yumi
defn: the tall asymmetrical Japanese bow laminated from bamboo and wood, made by bowyers (yumi-shi) for archery and kyūdō: Miyakonojō daikyū, lacquered and rattan-bound Edo bows.

label: Gakgung
defn: the Korean composite horn bow of horn, bamboo and sinew glued with isinglass and covered in birch bark, Joseon period to the present; its makers designated gungsi (1971).

label: German Gothic Armour
defn: south German plate armour of c. 1420–1530 from Augsburg, Nuremberg, Landshut and Innsbruck, with fluted, cusped and etched plates, passing into the Maximilian style: Gothic harnesses, sallets, Maximilian fluted armour.
aliases: Gothic armour; Maximilian armour; German armour

label: Japanese Armour
defn: samurai armour of laced lacquered scales and plates from the Heian to the Edo period, with helmets and face masks by armourer schools such as the Myōchin: ō-yoroi, dō-maru, tōsei gusoku, kabuto, menpō.

label: Fatimid Jewellery
defn: gold jewellery of Fatimid Egypt and Syria (10th–12th century) in filigree and granulation, often enamelled.

label: Mughal Jewellery
defn: jewellery and jewelled objects of the Mughal court: kundan setting, enamelled (minakari) backs, carved emeralds and jade inlaid with gems.

label: Bedouin Jewellery
defn: the silver jewellery of the Bedouin and settled peoples of Arabia, Yemen and Oman, worked in filigree, granulation and with coral and carnelian.

label: Berber Jewellery
defn: the silver jewellery of the Amazigh peoples of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia: fibulae, headdresses and the cloisonné enamel of Kabylia.

label: Javanese Gold Jewellery
defn: Gold ornaments of Hindu-Buddhist Java (8th–15th century), cast, repoussé and set with stones: sacred-thread clasps, ear ornaments, rings with Sri inscriptions, Wonoboyo hoard.

label: Miao Silver Ornaments
defn: Silver headdresses, neck-rings and breastplates hammered and filigreed by Miao smiths of Guizhou for festival dress.

label: Jangdo
defn: Korean ornamental knives in silver, horn and wood worn on the hanbok as accessory and symbol of fidelity; makers designated jangdojang.

label: Tairona Goldwork
defn: Cast gold and tumbaga ornaments of the Tairona of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (c. 900–1600 CE): bat-man and eagle pendants, nose ornaments, labrets.

label: Quimbaya Goldwork
defn: The gold of the Quimbaya of the Middle Cauca valley, with its ceramics: Quimbaya Treasure poporos, seated figures, helmets.

label: Calima Goldwork
defn: Hammered and cast gold of the Calima region of south-western Colombia in its Ilama, Yotoco and Malagana phases: diadems, nose rings, pectorals with faces.

label: Tolima Goldwork
defn: Flat cast gold pendants of the Tolima region of the Magdalena valley, with anchor-shaped human-bat figures.

label: Isthmian Goldwork
defn: Cast and hammered gold and tumbaga ornaments of the chiefdoms of Panama and Costa Rica (c. 200–1500 CE) in the Coclé, Veraguas, Chiriquí and Diquís styles: Sitio Conte plaques, eagle pendants, crocodile deity figures.

label: Mixtec Goldwork
defn: Lost-wax cast gold ornaments of the Postclassic Mixtec of Oaxaca, with filigree-effect wax threads: Monte Albán Tomb 7 pectorals, labrets, bell pendants.

label: Mapuche Silverwork
defn: The silver jewellery of Mapuche women in Chile and Argentina, flourishing from the 18th century: trapelacucha pectorals, tupu pins, trarilonco headbands.

label: Navajo Silverwork
defn: Silver jewellery and horse gear of Diné smiths since the 1850s, hammered, cast in tufa and stamped, set with turquoise from the 1880s: concho belts, squash blossom necklaces, ketohs, cuff bracelets.

label: Zuni Jewelry
defn: Lapidary jewellery of Zuni Pueblo, silver set with small cut stones since the 1920s: needlepoint and petit point, channel inlay, mosaic inlay.

label: Heishe
defn: Fine disc beads ground from shell, turquoise and stone and strung in necklaces, above all at Kewa (Santo Domingo) Pueblo.

label: Trade Silver
defn: Silver and later German-silver ornaments of the fur trade and of Native smiths of the Northeast, Great Lakes and Prairies (18th–19th century): ring and luckenbooth brooches, gorgets, armbands and hair plates.

label: Riji
defn: Pearl-shell pendants and pubic coverings of the Kimberley, engraved with interlocking meanders and filled with ochre, worn in ceremony and traded far inland: riji, jakoli, longkalongka.

label: Fabergé
defn: The jewellery and objets de luxe of the House of Fabergé in St Petersburg and Moscow, 1842–1918, in guilloché enamel, gold and hardstone: Imperial Easter eggs, cigarette cases, hardstone animals.

label: Hairwork
defn: Jewellery and pictures worked from human hair, a 19th-century fashion carried on as a village craft in Vamhus, Dalarna.

label: Temple Jewellery
defn: gold jewellery set with red and green stones, first made to adorn the deities of South Indian temples and now worn by brides and Bharatanatyam dancers, centred on Nagercoil (GI): jhumka, oddiyanam waist belts, nethi chutti.
aliases: temple jewellery of Nagercoil; Nagercoil temple jewellery

label: Thewa
defn: the Rajput craft of Pratapgarh in Rajasthan, from the 18th century, of fusing finely chased 23-carat gold sheet onto coloured glass: pendants, jewellery boxes, plaques with hunting and Krishna scenes.

label: Tarakasi
defn: the silver filigree of Cuttack in Odisha, of fine drawn wire shaped and soldered by hand: filigree ornaments, brooches, temple decorations for Durga Puja.
aliases: Cuttack filigree; tarkashi; Odisha silver filigree

label: Hopi Silverwork
defn: silver jewellery of Hopi smiths, from the late 1930s worked in the overlay technique developed with the Museum of Northern Arizona, a cut-out top sheet soldered over a darkened base: overlay bracelets, belt buckles, bolo ties.

label: Taxco Silver
defn: the silver jewellery and silverware of Taxco in Guerrero, revived from 1931 by William Spratling's workshops and carried on by his pupils: Los Castillo, Antonio Pineda, Hector Aguilar.
aliases: Mexican silver; Mexican modernist silver; Taxco silverwork

label: Kanzashi
defn: Japanese hair ornaments of lacquered wood, tortoiseshell, metal and folded silk worn with traditional coiffures, from the Edo period to the present: tsumami kanzashi of folded silk squares, bira-bira, kushi combs.

label: Persian Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets of Iran, from the Safavid court carpets (the Ardabil carpet, hunting and vase carpets, Polonaise carpets) to the city, village and tribal rugs named by their centres and peoples (Tabriz, Kashan, Isfahan, Kerman, Heriz, Qashqai, Bakhtiari).

label: Anatolian Rug
defn: knotted-pile carpets of Anatolia from the Seljuq Konya carpets onward: animal carpets, the 'Holbein' and 'Lotto' carpets known from European paintings, Ushak star and medallion carpets, and the village rugs of Bergama, Konya and Ghiordes.
aliases: Turkish carpet; Ushak carpet; Holbein carpet; Lotto carpet

label: Mamluk Carpet
defn: carpets woven in Cairo under the Mamluks (late 15th–early 16th century) in red, green and blue with kaleidoscopic geometric fields.

label: Caucasian Carpet
defn: knotted-pile rugs of the Caucasus — Kazak, Karabagh, Shirvan, Kuba and the dragon carpets — and of the Azerbaijani schools.

label: Turkmen Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets and tent furnishings of the Turkmen tribes (Tekke, Yomut, Salor, Saryk, Ersari), with their tribal güls.

label: Baluch Rug
defn: dark-toned knotted rugs of the Baluch peoples of eastern Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

label: Afghan Rug
defn: knotted rugs of Afghanistan, including the war rugs woven since 1979 with weapons and maps.

label: Mughal Carpet
defn: knotted carpets of the Mughal workshops of Lahore, Agra and Kashmir (late 16th–17th century): pictorial and flowering-plant carpets of very fine weave.

label: Moroccan Rug
defn: the pile and flatwoven rugs of the Amazigh tribes of Morocco (Beni Ouarain, Azilal, Boucherouite) and of the urban workshops of Rabat.

label: Freest Fisherman's Carpets
defn: Knotted carpets designed and made since the 1920s on the coast of the Bay of Greifswald (Freest, Western Pomerania), with motifs of fish, birds and sea.

label: Ryijy
defn: Finnish knotted-pile wall hangings and bed covers with a long shaggy pile, from 18th-century folk ryijys to modern artist-designed rugs.

label: Chinese Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets of China from the 17th century: Ningxia and Baotou carpets for monasteries and court, pillar carpets, and the Peking and Tianjin export rugs with relief-clipped pile, including the Art Deco 'Nichols' rugs.
aliases: Chinese rug; Ningxia carpet; Peking rug; Tianjin rug; Nichols rug

label: Tibetan Rug
defn: pile rugs of Tibet woven with the looped Tibetan knot for sitting, sleeping, meditation and saddles, peaking in the 19th–early 20th century and revived by exile workshops in Nepal and India: khaden, tiger rugs, Wangden warp-faced-back rugs.
aliases: Tibetan carpet; khaden; tiger rug; Wangden rug

label: Savonnerie Carpet
defn: knotted-pile carpets of the royal Savonnerie manufactory at Chaillot, Paris (1615–1825, then at the Gobelins), woven in the Turkish knot to court designs: the Grande Galerie carpets of the Louvre for Louis XIV.
aliases: Savonnerie; Savonnerie manufactory; tapis de la Savonnerie

label: Kilim
defn: tapestry-woven flatweaves of Anatolia, Iran, the Caucasus, Central Asia and North Africa, from slit-tapestry Anatolian kilims to Persian gelims, gabbeh-like tribal weaves and Tunisian mergoum.

label: Soumak
defn: weft-wrapped flatweaves of the Caucasus and north-west Iran, with a herringbone surface.

label: Al Sadu
defn: the warp-faced weaving of the Bedouin of Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, for tents and camel trappings (UNESCO 2011).

label: Inca Textiles
defn: The tapestry-woven cumbi cloth of the Inca state, woven by aqllakuna and cumbicamayoc, with tocapu tunics as the highest rank: Dumbarton Oaks tocapu tunic, checkerboard military tunics.

label: Wari Textiles
defn: The interlocking tapestry tunics of the Wari state (c. 600–1000 CE) with abstracted staff-god profiles expanded and compressed across the field.

label: Colonial Andean Tapestry
defn: Tapestry-woven textiles of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) in which cumbi weavers combined Inca, Spanish and Asian designs: colonial uncus with tocapu, tapices with coats of arms.

label: Andean Textiles
defn: The living warp-faced and complementary-warp weaving of Quechua and Aymara communities of Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador, with named regional styles: Jalq'a and Tarabuco axsus, Chinchero lliclla, Otavalo weaving.

label: Taquile Textile Art
defn: The weaving and knitting of Taquile Island in Lake Titicaca, where men knit chullos and women weave belts (chumpi) recording the agricultural calendar, inscribed by UNESCO in 2008.

label: Saltillo Serape
defn: Tapestry-woven wool blankets of Saltillo and northern Mexico (18th–19th century) with a central diamond medallion and serrated fields.

label: Navajo Weaving
defn: Tapestry-woven blankets and rugs of Diné women on the upright loom: chief's blankets (first to third phase), eye-dazzlers, Two Grey Hills and Ganado rugs, Yeibichai rugs.

label: Chilkat Weaving
defn: Twined mountain-goat-wool and cedar-bark robes, tunics and aprons of the Tlingit and Haida, woven from painted pattern boards in formline designs.

label: Coast Salish Weaving
defn: Twill and twined blankets of mountain-goat and dog wool woven by Coast Salish women on two-bar looms, revived since the 1960s.

label: Chimayó Weaving
defn: Hispano wool weaving of the upper Rio Grande valley, New Mexico, from colonial Rio Grande blankets to the Chimayó blankets and vests woven by families such as the Ortegas and Trujillos.

label: Māori Weaving
defn: The fibre arts of the Māori in harakeke (New Zealand flax) and muka (its fibre): finger-twined (whatu) cloaks with tāniko borders and plaited (raranga) baskets and mats: kaitaka and korowai cloaks, piupiu, kete, whāriki.

label: Ceinture Fléchée
defn: The finger-woven wool sash of French Canada and the Métis, with its arrow (flèche) and lightning patterns, an element of Quebec's intangible heritage: Assomption sashes.

label: Raanu
defn: Finnish weft-faced flatwoven wool coverlet and wall hanging in stripes and geometric patterns.

label: Chiprovtsi Kilim
defn: Tapestry-woven kilims of Chiprovtsi in north-western Bulgaria since the 17th century, with geometric and later floral designs (UNESCO 2014).

label: Pirot Kilim
defn: Double-sided tapestry-woven kilims of Pirot in south-eastern Serbia, with geometric motifs such as the turtle and the vine.

label: Sjenica-Pešter Kilim
defn: Kilims woven on the Pešter plateau around Sjenica in south-western Serbia.

label: Stapar Rugs
defn: Rug-making in the village of Stapar in Vojvodina (Serbia), with floral rugs on dark grounds.

label: Kotsy
defn: Ukrainian woollen flatwoven carpets (kots, kylym) of the Left-Bank and Polissia regions.

label: Reshetylivka Carpets
defn: Handwoven floral carpets of Reshetylivka in Poltava Oblast (Ukraine).

label: Romanian and Moldovan Wall Carpets
defn: Woollen wall carpets (scoarțe, covoare) woven in Romania and the Republic of Moldova and hung in houses as dowry and decoration (UNESCO 2016).

label: Tiraz
defn: inscribed textiles from the caliphal workshops (tiraz) of the Umayyads, Abbasids and Fatimids, with bands of embroidered or tapestry-woven Arabic inscriptions.

label: Safavid Silk Textiles
defn: the figured silks, lampas, brocades and velvets of Safavid Iran (Ghiyath al-Din 'Ali-yi Naqshband), with figural scenes and floral fields.

label: Ottoman Silk Textiles
defn: the silk lampas (kemha) and velvets (çatma) of Bursa and Istanbul (15th–17th century), with ogival lattices, tulips and çintamani.

label: Nasrid Silk
defn: silks woven in Nasrid Granada and Almería (13th–15th century), with interlace, inscriptions and the 'Alhambra silks'.

label: Termeh
defn: Persian tapestry-twill woven with the boteh, made in Yazd and Kerman.

label: Kashmir Shawl
defn: twill-tapestry shawls woven from pashmina in Kashmir (17th–19th century), whose boteh became the paisley of European imitations.

label: Banarasi Brocade
defn: Silk brocades woven with gold and silver zari in Varanasi, from Mughal kinkhab to the Banarasi sari: kinkhab, jangla and butidar saris.

label: Jamdani
defn: Supplementary-weft figured muslin of Dhaka and Bengal (UNESCO 2013), with motifs inlaid by hand on the loom: jamdani saris, Dhaka muslin.

label: Kanchipuram Silk
defn: Heavy mulberry-silk saris of Kanchipuram with contrast korvai borders and temple motifs.

label: Paithani
defn: Silk and zari saris of Paithan and Yeola in Maharashtra with tapestry-woven peacock and lotus pallus.

label: Songket
defn: Silk or cotton brocade with supplementary weft of gold and silver thread, woven in the Malay courts of Sumatra, the Peninsula and Brunei: Palembang songket, Minangkabau songket.

label: Lampung Ship Cloths
defn: Supplementary-weft ceremonial cloths of the Lampung of south Sumatra depicting ships of the soul: the large aristocratic palepai banners and the ubiquitous tampan.

label: Piña
defn: Sheer cloth woven from pineapple-leaf fibre in Aklan and Manila, often embroidered (calado), made into barong and pañuelo.

label: Inabel
defn: The cotton handloom weaving of the Ilocos region of Luzon, in binakol whirlpool and other patterns.

label: Naga Motif Weaving in Lao Communities
defn: Handwoven Lao silks with naga serpent motifs in supplementary weft and ikat (UNESCO 2023): sinh skirts, pha biang shoulder cloths.

label: Kesi
defn: Silk tapestry woven with discontinuous wefts in China from the Tang, reproducing paintings and calligraphy in the Song and dressing the Qing court: Shen Zifan's kesi landscapes, dragon robes.

label: Zhuang Brocade
defn: Weft-patterned cotton-and-silk brocade of the Zhuang of Guangxi, one of China's four famous brocades.

label: Li Textiles
defn: The spinning, ikat-dyeing, weaving and embroidery of the Li (Hlai) women of Hainan (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2009): tube skirts, dragon quilts.

label: Shuri Weaving
defn: The court textiles of Shuri, the Ryukyu capital: hanaori and rōton-ori figured weaves and kasuri silks.

label: Bashōfu
defn: Cloth woven from Japanese banana fibre in Okinawa and Amami, plain or kasuri-patterned, centred on Kijoka.

label: Echigo-jōfu and Ojiya-chijimi
defn: Fine ramie cloth of the Uonuma region of Niigata, snow-bleached and often kasuri-patterned (UNESCO 2009).

label: Hansan Mosi
defn: Fine ramie cloth woven by women of Hansan in South Chungcheong (UNESCO 2011), for summer hanbok.

label: Kente Cloth
defn: Strip-woven silk and cotton cloth of the Asante and Ewe of Ghana and Togo, narrow strips with named warp and weft-float patterns sewn edge to edge: adwini asa, oyokoman, Ewe kente.

label: Aso Oke
defn: Prestige strip-woven cloth of the Yoruba of Nigeria: sanyan, alaari, etu.

label: Akwete Cloth
defn: Cloth woven by Ndoki Igbo women of Akwete on the vertical loom, with the ikaki (tortoise) motif.

label: Ivorian Loincloth Weaving
defn: The traditional loincloth (pagne) weaving of Côte d'Ivoire, strip-woven on narrow looms (Baule, Senufo, Dioula, Dan), inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

label: Coptic Textiles
defn: Tapestry-woven linen and wool textiles of late antique and early Islamic Egypt, 3rd–8th century, from burial grounds: tunic clavi and roundels, hangings with Dionysiac and Nilotic scenes, weft-loop wall hangings.

label: Maya Textiles
defn: The backstrap-woven and brocaded cotton cloth of the Maya of Guatemala and Chiapas, whose huipiles, sashes and headcloths are distinct by town and community: Chichicastenango huipiles, Santiago Atitlán tzutes, Chamula wool.

label: Chancay Textiles
defn: Cotton and camelid cloth of the Chancay culture of Peru's central coast (c. 1000–1470 CE): gauze and openwork, painted cloth and woven dolls: gauze panels, painted cloths.

label: Flemish Tapestry
defn: Tapestry woven in the Southern Netherlands, 14th–17th century, at Arras, Tournai, Brussels, Oudenaarde and Antwerp, after cartoons by leading painters: Apocalypse of Angers, Unicorn tapestries, Acts of the Apostles after Raphael.

label: Aubusson Tapestry
defn: Tapestry and carpet weaving of Aubusson and Felletin in the Creuse, from the 16th century to its 20th-century revival (Lurçat), inscribed by UNESCO in 2009.

label: Täkänä
defn: Finnish double-weave (Finn-pick) technique giving reversible two-colour cloth, used for coverlets and hangings.

label: Northern Vidzeme Double-Weave Blankets
defn: Double-weave colour-gradient blanket weaving of Northern Vidzeme in Latvia.

label: Sigulda Belts
defn: Patterned belts woven in Sigulda municipality (Latvia).

label: Bezdan Damask
defn: Damask linen woven in Bezdan (Vojvodina, Serbia) since the 1880s, with pictorial and floral designs.

label: Serpanok Weaving
defn: Weaving of serpanok, a fine gauze-like cloth, in Dubrovytsia hromada (Rivne Oblast, Ukraine).

label: Hlyniany Textile
defn: Patterned woven textiles of Hlyniany (Lviv Oblast, Ukraine), long known for its kilims.

label: Obukhovychi Weaving
defn: Traditional patterned weaving of the village of Obukhovychi (Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine).

label: Gobelins Tapestry
defn: Tapestry woven at the royal Gobelins Manufactory in Paris from 1662 under Le Brun, the official weaving of the French crown (The History of the King, Les Maisons royales, the Boucher Loves of the Gods).

label: Beauvais Tapestry
defn: Tapestry woven at the Beauvais Manufactory from 1664, the private royal works for furniture covers and lighter subjects after Oudry and Boucher (Fêtes italiennes, Chinese Series).

label: Chanderi
defn: the sheer silk and cotton handloom weaving of Chanderi in Madhya Pradesh, with small supplementary-weft butis and zari borders, for saris and dupattas.

label: Maheshwari
defn: the light silk-and-cotton handloom saris of Maheshwar on the Narmada, with reversible borders and chatai, eent and other geometric motifs, revived in the 18th century under Ahilyabai Holkar.

label: Mangalagiri
defn: the pit-loom cotton weaving of Mangalagiri in Andhra Pradesh, plain-bodied saris and fabrics with Nizam-pattern zari borders.

label: Tangaliya
defn: the weaving of the Dangasia community of Surendranagar in Saurashtra, Gujarat, in which extra yarn is twisted around the warp to make raised bead-like dots (dana) forming geometric figures on wool and cotton shawls.

label: Kasavu
defn: the handloom weaving of Kerala, off-white cotton saris and mundu with fine gold or silver zari borders, centred on Balaramapuram.

label: Kota Doria
defn: the open-check cotton-and-silk weaving of Kaithun near Kota in Rajasthan, whose square khat pattern makes a translucent cloth for saris.

label: Nishijin-ori
defn: the figured silk weaving of the Nishijin district of Kyoto, for the court and aristocracy since the Heian period and today chiefly obi and kimono cloth, in brocade, damask, tsuzure and gold-thread weaves.

label: Acheik
defn: the Burmese tapestry-woven silk of Amarapura, its wave patterns made with up to a hundred small shuttles, for court and wedding longyi and htamein.

label: Shemma
defn: the Ethiopian narrow-loom weaving of hand-spun cotton by men of the highlands, with woven tilet and tibeb borders, made into the netela, gabi and habesha kemis: Shiro Meda, Dorze weaving.
aliases: shemma weaving; tibeb; tilet; Habesha weaving

label: Oaxacan Textiles
defn: the backstrap-woven and embroidered textiles of the Indigenous peoples of Oaxaca, Mexico, distinct by community: Amuzgo huipiles of Xochistlahuaca, Chinantec huipiles of Ojitlán, Tehuantepec Zapotec dress.

label: Tartan
defn: the twill-woven wool cloth of Scotland patterned in crossing coloured stripes (setts), from Highland district tartans to the clan, dress and regimental setts recorded since the 19th century: Black Watch, Royal Stewart.

label: Tweed
defn: the rough woollen twills and herringbones of Scotland and Ireland, dyed and spun with flecked colour and woven in named regional cloths: Harris Tweed, Donegal tweed.

label: Faso Dan Fani
defn: the strip-woven hand-spun cotton cloth of Burkina Faso, spun and dyed by women and woven in narrow bands on horizontal looms, promoted as national dress from 1983.

label: Welsh Tapestry
defn: reversible double-cloth woollen blankets and bedspreads woven by the mills of Wales from the 19th century, in geometric and jacquard panel designs: Caernarfon pattern blankets of Trefriw and Melin Tregwynt.
aliases: Welsh tapestry blanket; Welsh double weave; carthen

label: Trade Blankets
defn: wool blankets and robes woven by Euro-American mills for trade with Native American and First Nations peoples, from striped point blankets to the jacquard-woven designs adopted as prestige dress and gifts: Pendleton and Beacon blankets, the Chief Joseph pattern, Hudson's Bay point blankets.
aliases: Native American trade blanket; Indian trade blanket; Pendleton blanket; camp blanket

label: Peshtemal
defn: flat-woven cotton and linen bath wraps of the Ottoman hammam woven on hand looms in regional stripe and check patterns, at Buldan, Denizli and formerly Antioch.
aliases: pestamal; peştamal; Turkish towel; hammam towel

label: Irish Linen
defn: linen weaving of Ulster and Ireland from the 17th century, above all the jacquard-woven figured damask of Lisburn, Banbridge and Belfast for table linen.

label: Basque Linen
defn: striped linen of the French Basque Country and Béarn, first woven by itinerant weavers as mantes à bœufs for cattle and now as table and kitchen linen with seven coloured bands.
aliases: linge basque; toile basque; mante à bœufs

label: Suzani
defn: large embroidered hangings and covers of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan (Bukhara, Nurata, Samarkand, Shakhrisabz), worked in silk chain and couching stitch.

label: Ottoman Embroidery
defn: the silk and metal-thread embroidery of Ottoman households and court: towels, napkins, covers and garments, worked in double running and satin stitch.

label: Palestinian Embroidery
defn: tatreez: the cross-stitch embroidery of Palestinian women's dress by village and region (UNESCO 2021).

label: Pateh
defn: the wool embroidery of Kerman in Iran, densely covering woollen cloth with boteh and floral designs.

label: Rasht Embroidery
defn: felt appliqué and chain-stitch embroidery of Rasht in Gilan (Iran).

label: Oya
defn: Turkish needle lace: knotted borders of flowers for headscarves.

label: Khayamiya
defn: the appliqué tent panels of the Cairo tentmakers' street, Sharia al-Khayamiya.

label: Balochi Needlework
defn: the dense geometric embroidery of Baloch women's dress (Iran, Pakistan, Afghanistan).

label: Phulkari
defn: Darn-stitch silk embroidery on khaddar of the women of Punjab, in sparse phulkari and fully covered bagh: bagh, chope.

label: Chikankari
defn: White-on-white shadow and knot-stitch embroidery of Lucknow on fine cotton.

label: Kantha
defn: Running-stitch embroidery on layered old cloth by the women of Bengal and Bangladesh: nakshi kantha, lep kantha.

label: Sujani
defn: Running-stitch embroidered quilts of Bhusura in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, with narrative figures.

label: Ralli Quilt
defn: Patchwork, applique and embroidered quilts of Sindh, Cholistan, Kutch and Rajasthan.

label: Chakan
defn: The silk-on-cotton floral embroidery of Tajikistan for garments, coverlets and wall hangings (UNESCO 2018): chakan dresses, wall hangings.

label: Khamak
defn: The fine geometric satin-stitch embroidery of Kandahar and of Hazara women in Afghanistan, worked from the back on fine cotton: shirt panels, pillow covers, shawls.

label: Turkmen Needlework
defn: The embroidery applied to Turkmen dress of all ages and sexes in Turkmenistan and Iran, in chain, satin and stitch-band techniques (UNESCO 2022): chyrpy mantles, tahya caps.

label: Tapis
defn: The ceremonial tube skirts of Lampung women, warp-ikat and woven grounds couched with gold thread, mica and embroidery.

label: Kalaga
defn: Burmese padded appliqué hangings embroidered with sequins and metal thread in scenes from the Jatakas and court life.

label: Tekat
defn: Malay raised gold-thread embroidery couched over card or padding, for cushions, betel covers and wedding furnishings.

label: Suzhou Embroidery
defn: Silk embroidery of Suzhou in Jiangsu, one of China's four famous embroideries, fine-split thread and double-sided pieces: cats, goldfish, painting copies.

label: Xiang Embroidery
defn: Silk embroidery of Changsha in Hunan, one of the four famous embroideries, famed for tigers and lions in shaded stitches.

label: Shu Embroidery
defn: Silk embroidery of Chengdu in Sichuan, one of the four famous embroideries: pandas, carp and hibiscus on satin.

label: Cantonese Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of the Pearl River Delta (Guangzhou and Chaozhou), dense and brilliant, with raised gold-thread work; one of the four famous embroideries.

label: Gu Embroidery
defn: Painting-embroidery of the Gu family of Shanghai (late Ming), copying Song and Yuan paintings in silk thread: Han Ximeng's albums.

label: Korean Embroidery
defn: Silk embroidery of Joseon court and household (jasu): embroidered screens, rank badges (hyungbae), pillow ends, wedding robes (hwarot); masters designated jasujang.

label: Bojagi
defn: Korean wrapping cloths, above all jogakbo patchwork of leftover ramie and silk, and embroidered subo.

label: Sashiko
defn: Japanese running-stitch quilting and darning of indigo cloth, in regional forms: kogin of Tsugaru, hishizashi, mended boro.

label: Hmong Textile Art
defn: Embroidery, batik, appliqué and pleating of the Miao (Hmong) of Guizhou and the Hmong diaspora: pleated skirts, baby carriers, story cloths (paj ntaub).

label: Ainu Textiles
defn: Ainu robes of elm-bark (attus) and nettle cloth and of imported cotton, with appliqué and chain-stitch embroidery of curving designs: ruunpe, chikarkarpe, kaparamip.

label: Kuba Raffia Textiles
defn: Raffia cloth of the Kuba peoples of the DR Congo, woven by men and embroidered by women: Shoowa cut-pile ('Kasai velvet') panels, appliqué overskirts, Bushoong ceremonial skirts.

label: Asafo Flags
defn: Appliqué regimental flags (frankaa) of the Fante Asafo companies of coastal Ghana, with proverb designs and a corner Union Jack or Ghanaian flag.

label: Paracas Textiles
defn: Camelid-wool embroidered mantles from the Paracas Necropolis on Peru's south coast (c. 300 BCE–200 CE), stem-stitched with repeating flying figures: Paracas Necropolis mantles.

label: Mola
defn: Reverse-appliqué cotton panels made by Guna women of Panama and Colombia for the front and back of their blouses.

label: Arpillera
defn: Appliqué and embroidered burlap-backed pictures made by women's workshops in Chile under the Pinochet dictatorship and later in Peru.

label: Drapo Vodou
defn: Sequinned and beaded ritual flags of Haitian Vodou, carried to salute the lwa: vèvè flags, Myrlande Constant tapestries.

label: Ñandutí
defn: Paraguayan needle lace of radiating spider-web suns, made in Itauguá.

label: Divina Pastora Irish Lace
defn: The needle lace (renda irlandesa) made with cord and buttonhole stitches in Divina Pastora, Sergipe, registered by IPHAN.

label: Seminole Patchwork
defn: Machine-pieced bands of cotton strips sewn into skirts, jackets and shirts by Seminole and Miccosukee women of Florida since the early 20th century.

label: Ribbonwork
defn: Silk-ribbon appliqué cut and layered in negative and positive designs on skirts, leggings and blankets by Great Lakes and Prairie peoples (Menominee, Ho-Chunk, Meskwaki, Potawatomi, Osage) since the late 18th century.

label: Moosehair Embroidery
defn: Embroidery in dyed moosehair on birchbark and black cloth by Wendat (Huron) women of Wendake (Lorette) and other Northeastern peoples, learned from Ursuline nuns: floral moccasins, calling-card boxes, cigar cases.

label: Star Quilts
defn: Pieced quilts centred on a single eight-pointed star of diamond patches, made by Lakota, Dakota and other Plains women since the reservation era and given at honouring and memorial giveaways.

label: Tivaevae
defn: The appliqué and piecework quilts of the Cook Islands (and tīfaifai of Tahiti), sewn communally by women's groups (vainetini) and given at weddings, birthdays and funerals: tivaevae manu, tivaevae taorei, tivaevae tataura.

label: Opus Anglicanum
defn: English medieval embroidery in silk and gold thread, c. 1200–1400, prized across Europe for vestments: Syon Cope, Butler-Bowdon Cope, Steeple Aston Cope.

label: Bucks Point Lace
defn: English bobbin lace of Buckinghamshire and the East Midlands, 18th–19th century, a point-ground lace in the manner of Lille and Mechlin.

label: Bedfordshire Lace
defn: English bobbin lace of the Midlands from the mid-19th century, a guipure lace of plaits and leaves influenced by Maltese lace.

label: Amish Quilts
defn: Pieced quilts of the Amish of Pennsylvania and the Midwest, c. 1870–1950, in solid dark colours and bold geometric fields with fine quilting: Center Diamond, Bars, Sunshine and Shadow.

label: Hooked Rugs
defn: Rugs and mats made by hooking strips of cloth or yarn through a backing, in New England and the Canadian Maritimes from the 19th century, including the Grenfell mats of Labrador and Newfoundland.

label: Greek Island Embroidery
defn: The silk-on-linen embroidery of the Aegean and Ionian islands and Epirus (17th–19th century), each island with its own stitches and designs, used for bed curtains, cushions and dress: Cretan skirt borders, Rhodian bed tents, Naxos and Dodecanese hangings.

label: Hardanger Embroidery
defn: Norwegian whitework of counted satin-stitch blocks (kloster) with cut and drawn threads, from the Hardanger district, used on bunad aprons and linens.

label: Mountmellick Embroidery
defn: Irish white embroidery of raised floral designs in thick cotton on white cotton satin, begun in Mountmellick, County Laois, about 1825 by Johanna Carter.

label: Arraiolos Rug
defn: Portuguese wool rugs embroidered in Slav (long-armed cross) stitch on linen or jute canvas, made in Arraiolos in the Alentejo since the 17th century.

label: Bordados da Glória do Ribatejo
defn: The embroidery of Glória do Ribatejo (Salvaterra de Magos), worked mainly in cross stitch on household linens and local dress.

label: Alençon Lace
defn: French needle lace of Alençon in Normandy, developed in the 1660s under royal patronage and made into the 19th century, with fine réseau ground and corded outlines: flounces, lappets.

label: Burano Lace
defn: Venetian needle lace of the island of Burano, revived in 1872 by the Burano lace school on the model of the old Venetian points.

label: Lefkara Lace
defn: The drawn-thread and needle-lace embroidery of Pano Lefkara in Cyprus, worked on linen in geometric designs (UNESCO 2009).

label: Brussels Lace
defn: Pillow lace of Brussels and Brabant, its motifs made separately in bobbin or needle lace and joined to a droschel or bride ground (17th–19th century), including point de gaze and Brussels appliqué.

label: Mechlin Lace
defn: Flemish bobbin lace of Mechelen with a hexagonal ground and a flat thread outlining the motifs, the 18th century's favourite lace for ruffles.

label: Quill Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of leather with split quills of peacock tail feathers on belts, braces and shoes of Alpine dress, practised in Tyrol (Sarntal) and Austria.

label: Honiton Lace
defn: English bobbin lace of east Devon whose motifs are made separately and joined, famed for Queen Victoria's wedding lace (1840).

label: Le Puy Lace
defn: Bobbin lace of Le Puy-en-Velay in the Auvergne, in linen, silk and wool guipures and Cluny-style laces made by cottage lacemakers.

label: Maltese Lace
defn: Bobbin lace of Malta and Gozo, above all the 19th-century silk guipure with the Maltese cross and wheatears.

label: Headford Lace
defn: The bobbin lace of Headford, County Galway, a cottage industry of the 18th–19th centuries revived today.

label: Carrickmacross Lace
defn: Irish appliqué lace of County Monaghan, cambric shapes cut and sewn on machine net, introduced about 1820 by Mrs Grey Porter.

label: Limerick Lace
defn: Irish embroidered net lace of Limerick (from 1829), worked in tambour (chain stitch) or run (darning) stitch on machine net.

label: Irish Crochet Lace
defn: Crochet made in imitation of Venetian needle lace, spread as famine relief from the 1840s; motifs are worked separately and joined with a crocheted mesh: Clones lace, Youghal-area crochet.

label: Ukrainian Embroidery
defn: The regional embroidery of Ukraine on shirts (vyshyvanka), rushnyky and household linen in cross, satin and counted stitches, distinct by region and village: Reshetylivka white-on-white, Borshchiv black shirts, Podillia nyz.

label: Rushnyk
defn: East Slavic ritual cloths of linen embroidered or woven with symbolic red and black ornament, used at weddings, funerals and to dress icons: Krolevets woven rushnyky.

label: Belarusian Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of Belarus on ritual towels, shirts and aprons in counted red geometric ornament, including the Vetka negliubka tradition.

label: Chuvash Embroidery
defn: Counted-thread embroidery of the Chuvash of the Volga in red, black and green on white linen, for headdresses, shirts and ritual cloths.

label: Mari Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of the Mari of the Volga-Kama region, dense red-and-black geometric patterns on shirts and headdresses (shurka, shymaksh).

label: Karelian Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of the Karelians of Finland and Russia, in red counted and drawn work on towels and shirts.

label: Krestets Stitch
defn: Drawn-thread whitework embroidery of Krestsy (Novgorod region) on linen, with geometric openwork grounds.

label: Mstyora Embroidery
defn: White satin-stitch and openwork embroidery of Mstyora (Vladimir region) on batiste and linen.

label: Muhu Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of the Estonian island of Muhu, with bold floral motifs and birds in bright pinks, greens and oranges on black wool.

label: Matyó Embroidery
defn: The embroidery of the Matyó community of Mezőkövesd in Hungary, with dense roses and peonies in bright satin stitch (UNESCO 2012).
aliases: Folk art of the Matyó;Mezőkövesd embroidery

label: Zmijanje Embroidery
defn: Dark-blue wool embroidery on women's dress and household linen of the Zmijanje villages near Banja Luka (UNESCO 2014).

label: Macedonian Embroidery
defn: Embroidery of North Macedonia on women's shirts and sleeves in dense red, black and gold geometric motifs.

label: Kosovo-Style Embroidery
defn: Serbian embroidery in the Kosovo style, inscribed in the Serbian ICH inventory.

label: Altiță
defn: Embroidery on the shoulder band (altiță) of the Romanian and Moldovan traditional blouse (ie), the defining ornament of the costume (UNESCO 2022).

label: Syrian-Armenian Embroidery
defn: The embroidery culture of the Syrian-Armenian community of Armenia (Marash and Aintab traditions), inscribed in Armenia's ICH list.
aliases: Embroidery culture of the Syrian-Armenian community

label: Armenian Needlelace
defn: Knotted needle lace of Armenia and the Armenian diaspora, made with a needle in rows of knots for collars and covers.

label: Tatar Leather Mosaic
defn: The Kazan Tatar technique (kayuly kün) of stitching coloured morocco pieces into mosaic patterns with gold thread, for boots (ichigi) and slippers.

label: Orenburg Shawl
defn: Knitted lace shawls of goat down from the Orenburg region, including the fine gossamer 'web' shawl that passes through a ring.

label: Vologda Lace
defn: Bobbin tape lace of Vologda with continuous tape patterns on a net ground (from the 19th century).

label: Yelets Lace
defn: Fine bobbin tape lace of Yelets (Lipetsk region), with small motifs on delicate grounds.

label: Rauma Lace
defn: Bobbin lace of the town of Rauma in Finland, made since the 18th century with fine linen thread.

label: Lace-Making in Heinämaa
defn: The bobbin lace tradition of the village of Heinämaa in Finland.

label: Knipelēšana
defn: Latvian bobbin lace-making tradition.

label: Idrija Lace
defn: Bobbin tape lace of Idrija (Slovenia), made since the 17th century with a continuous tape (UNESCO 2018).

label: Lacemaking in Croatia
defn: The lace traditions of Croatia — needle lace of Pag, bobbin lace of Lepoglava and Sveta Marija, aloe-thread lace of Hvar (UNESCO 2009).

label: Venetian Lace
defn: The needle laces of Venice, 16th-18th century, from reticella and punto in aria to the sculptural gros point and rose point that dominated European fashion before French point d'Alençon: punto in aria collars, gros point de Venise flounces, rose point cravat ends.
aliases: Point de Venise;punto Venezia;Venetian needle lace;gros point de Venise

label: Quilting
defn: The British and American tradition of pieced (patchwork), appliquéd and whole-cloth quilts from the 18th century, named by pattern, region and type: Baltimore album quilts, Log Cabin and Star of Bethlehem quilts, crazy quilts, Harriet Powers's Bible quilts.

label: Quilts of Gee's Bend
defn: Quilts made by the women of Gee's Bend, Alabama, since the 19th century: Annie Mae Young's work-clothes quilts, Mary Lee Bendolph's quilts.

label: Aran Knitting
defn: the cabled hand-knitting of the Aran Islands off Co. Galway, worked in undyed báinín wool with cable, honeycomb, diamond and moss stitches, exported worldwide from the 1950s: Aran jumpers, geansaí Árann.
aliases: Aran sweater; Aran jumper; geansaí Árann

label: Gansey Knitting
defn: the close-knit seaman's jumpers of Guernsey and the British fishing coasts, knitted in the round in worsted with underarm gussets and textured yoke patterns that vary by village: Guernsey frocks, Filey and Cornish ganseys.
aliases: Guernsey knitting; guernsey; gansey; fisherman's gansey

label: Fair Isle Knitting
defn: stranded two-colour knitting of Fair Isle and Shetland, worked in the round in short floats with OXO and star bands, fashionable from 1921: Fair Isle jumpers, Shetland yoke sweaters.
aliases: Fair Isle; Shetland knitting; Shetland colourwork

label: Lopapeysa
defn: the Icelandic yoke sweater knitted seamless in unspun lopi wool with a patterned circular yoke, a national symbol since the mid-20th century.

label: Norwegian Knitting
defn: the regional two-colour stranded knitting of Norway, with lice stitches and embroidered bands: Setesdal lusekofte, Fana cardigans, Selbu mittens and the Selbu rose, and their 20th-century descendants.
aliases: lusekofte; Setesdal sweater; fanakofte; Norwegian colourwork knitting

label: Cowichan Knitting
defn: the heavy shawl-collar sweaters hand-knitted by Coast Salish women of the Cowichan Valley on Vancouver Island in hand-spun undyed wool with pictorial motifs, from the late 19th century.

label: Sukajan
defn: the densely embroidered souvenir jackets born around the US naval base at Yokosuka after 1945, their dragons, tigers and eagles worked by kimono embroiderers of Kiryū and Ashikaga.
aliases: sukajan embroidery; Yokosuka jumper; souvenir jacket

label: Nyonya Kebaya
defn: the embroidered voile kebaya of Peranakan women of Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, worked in machine and hand sulam with flowers and birds and fastened with linked kerongsang brooches.
aliases: kebaya nyonya; kebaya sulam; kebaya Peranakan

label: Majboud Embroidery
defn: the raised gold and silver thread embroidery of Algiers and other Algerian cities, couched over card or padding on velvet for the karakou, caftan and bridal furnishings.

label: Hausa Embroidery
defn: the hand embroidery of the robes (babban riga) of the Hausa aristocracy of Kano and Zaria, worked by men in silk or cotton on strip-woven cloth with the aska biyu (two knives) and spiral motifs.
aliases: babban riga embroidery; Hausa robe embroidery

label: Crewelwork
defn: embroidery in two-ply worsted wool on linen or linen-cotton twill, English from the early 17th century and carried to colonial America, with tree-of-life, flowering-branch and fanciful animal designs for bed hangings and curtains: Jacobean bed hangings, Deerfield crewelwork.
aliases: crewel embroidery; Jacobean embroidery; Jacobean crewelwork

label: Stumpwork
defn: English raised embroidery of c. 1650–1700 with padded and wire-supported figures, worked by girls on satin for pictures, mirror frames and caskets.
aliases: raised work; English stumpwork; embosted work

label: Berlin Wool Work
defn: needlepoint in tent and cross stitch with bright wool on canvas, worked from hand-coloured charts first printed in Berlin (1804), the dominant domestic embroidery of Europe and America until c. 1875.

label: Central Asian Ikat
defn: warp-ikat silks and silk-cotton (adras, atlas) of Bukhara, Samarkand and the Fergana Valley (abrband, 'cloud-binding').

label: Qalamkar
defn: block-printed and painted cotton of Isfahan.

label: Indian Chintz
defn: Mordant-painted and resist-dyed cottons made on the Coromandel Coast and in Gujarat for export to Europe and Asia, 17th–18th century: palampores, Golconda floorspreads, petticoat panels for the Dutch market.

label: Kalamkari
defn: Pen-drawn and block-printed mordant-dyed cotton of Andhra Pradesh, in the Srikalahasti temple-cloth and Machilipatnam block-print styles: temple hangings, Persian-market prayer cloths.

label: Ajrakh
defn: Indigo and madder resist block-printed cotton of Sindh and Kutch, printed on both faces.

label: Bandhani
defn: Tie-dyed textiles of Gujarat and Rajasthan made by binding thousands of tiny points: gharchola, odhni.

label: Leheriya
defn: Diagonally tied and dyed wave-patterned turbans and saris of Rajasthan.

label: Patola
defn: Double-ikat silk saris of Patan in Gujarat, traded to Southeast Asia as heirloom cloths.

label: Rogan Art
defn: Cloth painted with a thickened castor-oil paste drawn from a stylus, practised at Nirona in Kutch.

label: Indonesian Batik
defn: Wax-resist dyed cloth of Java (UNESCO 2009), drawn by canting (tulis) or stamped (cap), in the court styles of Yogyakarta and Surakarta and the coastal pesisir styles of Pekalongan, Lasem and Cirebon: parang rusak kain, batik Belanda, Hokokai batik.

label: Malaysian Batik
defn: Block-printed and hand-drawn batik of the east-coast Malay states, Kelantan and Terengganu, with large floral designs.

label: Indonesian Ikat
defn: Warp-ikat cotton cloths of the eastern islands and of Sumatra, Borneo and Sulawesi, tied and dyed in morinda and indigo: Sumba hinggi mantles, Toraja sacred cloths, Savu and Flores sarongs.

label: Geringsing
defn: The double-ikat cotton cloths of Tenganan Pegeringsingan in Bali, worn for protection in rites.

label: Tais
defn: Handwoven textiles of Timor-Leste (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2021), in ikat, supplementary weft and tapestry.

label: Pua Kumbu
defn: The ceremonial warp-ikat blankets of the Iban of Sarawak and Kalimantan, woven by women with spirit and ancestor figures.

label: T'nalak
defn: Abaca warp-ikat cloth of the T'boli of South Cotabato, its designs dreamed by the weaver.

label: Telepuk
defn: Malay cloth stamped with gold leaf from carved wooden blocks for court and wedding dress.

label: Yūzen
defn: Paste-resist dyeing with a fine rice-paste line and painted dyes, attributed to Miyazaki Yūzensai of Kyoto (late 17th century): Kyō-yūzen and Kaga-yūzen kimono.

label: Katazome
defn: Japanese stencil dyeing with paste applied through cut paper stencils (katagami), and the stencils themselves as collected objects: Ise-katagami, komon small-pattern kimono.

label: Bingata
defn: Okinawan stencil- and freehand paste-resist cloth dyed in bright pigments, made for the Ryukyu court and gentry.

label: Tsutsugaki
defn: Freehand paste-resist dyeing with a cone (tsutsu), mostly indigo, for festive covers, futon covers and banners (Edo to early 20th century).

label: Shibori
defn: Japanese shaped-resist dyeing by binding, stitching, folding and capping cloth: kanoko dots, arimatsu-narumi shibori, the Momoyama tsujigahana robes.

label: Kasuri
defn: Japanese ikat: cotton, ramie and silk cloth woven from resist-dyed threads, in regional centres: Kurume, Iyo, Bingo, Miyako-jōfu.

label: Bai Tie-Dye
defn: Indigo tie-dyed cotton (zharan) of the Bai of Dali and Zhoucheng in Yunnan.

label: Geumbak
defn: Korean gold-leaf stamping of textiles with carved woodblocks, for royal and bridal dress; makers designated geumbakjang.

label: Bògòlanfini
defn: Mud-dyed cotton cloth of the Bamana of Mali, strip-woven by men and painted by women with fermented mud on a leaf-dye ground.

label: Adire
defn: Indigo resist-dyed cloth of Yoruba women: adire eleko (starch resist), adire oniko (tied), adire alabere (stitched).

label: Adinkra Cloth
defn: Asante funerary and prestige cloth stamped with calabash stamps of named adinkra symbols, centred on Ntonso.

label: Ndop Cloth
defn: Indigo stitch-resist royal display cloth of the Cameroon Grassfields (Bamileke, Bamum), strip-woven and patterned in white.

label: Kanga
defn: Printed cotton cloths of the Swahili coast worn in pairs, with a border, central field and a printed Swahili proverb (jina): kanga, kitenge.

label: Rebozo
defn: The Mexican woman's shawl, at its finest in warp-ikat (jaspe) cotton and silk with knotted fringe from Santa María del Río and Tenancingo.

label: Blaudruck
defn: Resist block printing and indigo dyeing of linen and cotton, carried on by family dye-works of Central Europe (UNESCO 2018, Austria, Czechia, Germany, Hungary, Slovakia): Burgenland blueprint, Mühlviertel indigo printing.

label: Staphorster Stipwerk
defn: Dot printing of Staphorst in Overijssel: coloured patterns stamped with pin-headed stamps on cloth for the village dress (kraplap, caps).

label: Pavlovo Posad Shawl
defn: Printed woollen shawls of Pavlovo Posad (Moscow region) since the 1860s, with dense roses and borders, first block-printed then screen-printed.

label: Kelaghayi
defn: Silk headscarves of Azerbaijan (Sheki, Basqal) printed by wooden stamps with resist and natural dyes, with buta motifs (UNESCO 2014).

label: African Wax Prints
defn: Roller-printed cotton with a batik-like resin resist made in the Netherlands (Vlisco, from 1846), Britain and later West Africa for West and Central African markets, with named and commemorative designs: Vlisco Dutch wax samples, commemorative portrait cloths, Ankara fancy prints.

label: Khmer Silk Weaving
defn: the silk weaving of Cambodia for the sampot, above all the weft-ikat hol in uneven twill and the pictorial pidan hangings, with brocaded charobab: sampot hol, pidan.
aliases: hol; sampot hol; pidan; Cambodian silk

label: Shweshwe
defn: the indigo discharge-printed cotton of South Africa, roller-printed with small geometric and floral figures since the 19th century and taken into Basotho, Xhosa and Tswana dress.

label: Indian Ikat
defn: the single and double ikat of India other than Patan patola, tied and dyed in warp, weft or both before weaving: Pochampally ikat, telia rumal, Sambalpuri bandha.

label: Rajasthani Block Printing
defn: hand printing of cotton with carved wooden blocks by Chhipa printers near Jaipur since the 16th–17th century: Bagru dabu mud-resist prints on dark grounds, Sanganeri floral prints on white.
aliases: Bagru print; Sanganeri print; dabu; Chhipa printing

label: Indiennes
defn: block- and copperplate-printed cottons made in France and Europe after Indian chintz from the 17th century, banned in France 1686–1759: Provençal indiennes of Marseille and Tarascon, toile de Jouy of the Oberkampf manufactory.
aliases: indienne; Provençal prints; indiennes de Marseille; European printed cottons

label: Kyrgyz and Kazakh Felt
defn: the mosaic felt carpets (shyrdak), pressed felt (ala-kiyiz, tus kiiz) and embroidered felt of the Kyrgyz and Kazakh (UNESCO 2012).

label: Palestinian Costume
defn: the embroidered thobes and headdresses of Palestinian women, distinct by village and region.

label: Ottoman Court Dress
defn: the kaftans and garments of the Ottoman sultans and court, kept in the Topkapı Palace treasury.

label: Possum-Skin Cloak
defn: Cloaks of sewn possum pelts incised on the skin side with clan and Country designs, worn by the Aboriginal peoples of south-eastern Australia and revived since the 1990s: Lake Condah and Maiden's Punt cloaks, revival cloaks.

label: Gákti
defn: The dress of the Sámi, a tunic of wool or reindeer skin trimmed with woven bands and coloured cloth whose cut and colours mark region and family: Kautokeino gákti, four-winds hat.

label: Bunad
defn: The regional folk costumes of Norway, revived and standardised from local dress since the late 19th century, with embroidered bodices, aprons and silver brooches (sølje): Vest-Telemark bunad, Hardanger bunad.

label: Swedish Folk Costume
defn: The parish costumes of Sweden, worn and revived as signs of local and national identity, with embroidered bodices, pockets and headdresses: Dalarna costumes, Leksand and Rättvik dress.

label: Tracht
defn: The regional folk dress of the German-speaking Alps and southern Germany, made and worn in local forms with their own headdresses, bodices and embroidery: Bregenzerwald Juppe, Lake Constance Radhaube, Gailtal costume.

label: Traditional Albanian Clothing
defn: The regional folk costume of the Albanians, with distinct ensembles by region and community: xhubleta bell-shaped skirt, fustanella, xhamadan vests.

label: Croatian National Costume
defn: The regional folk costumes of Croatia, from Slavonian gold-embroidered dress to Dalmatian and Zagorje ensembles.

label: Macedonian Traditional Clothing
defn: The regional folk costumes of North Macedonia, with heavily embroidered women's shirts and sleeveless coats.

label: Erzya Costume
defn: The traditional dress of the Erzya (Mordvin) people, with embroidered white shirts (panar), pulai hip ornament and headdresses.

label: Kimono
defn: The Japanese T-shaped wrapped robe as a dress tradition, from the Momoyama and Edo kosode to the Meiji and modern kimono, with its named garment types and their dyed, woven and embroidered decoration: Edo-period kosode with Ōmi hakkei design, furisode, uchikake wedding robes, katabira summer robes.

label: Basotho Blanket
defn: the woollen blankets worn as cloaks by the Basotho of Lesotho and South Africa since the 1870s, whose named designs and pin-stripes mark rank, marriage and initiation: seanamarena, Victoria England, letlama.

label: Savile Row Tailoring
defn: the bespoke men's tailoring of Savile Row in London from the early 19th century, cut from a pattern drafted for each client and the model of the structured English suit: Henry Poole, Huntsman, Anderson & Sheppard.

label: Neapolitan Tailoring
defn: the soft tailoring school of Naples, with unpadded shoulders, spalla camicia sleeves and little or no lining, developed in the 20th century as the counterpart to Savile Row structure.

label: Qipao
defn: the Chinese woman's close-fitting dress of the 1920s onward, cut in Shanghai and Hong Kong with Western darts on the Manchu robe, with piped edges and knotted pankou fastenings.

label: Moroccan Caftan
defn: the ceremonial caftan and two-piece takchita of Moroccan women, tailored with sfifa braid and akaad knotted buttons and embroidered in silk and gold thread (UNESCO 2025).

label: Tlemcen Wedding Costume
defn: the bridal costume of Tlemcen in western Algeria, the chedda of velvet gold-embroidered caftan, conical crown and pearl jewellery, with the craftsmanship of its making (UNESCO 2012).

label: Highland Dress
defn: the dress of the Scottish Highlands and Isles worn as a curated national costume since the 18th century: belted plaid, kilt, sporran and plaid in tartan.

label: Pollera
defn: the national dress of Panama from the Azuero Peninsula, a gala skirt and blouse of white cloth worked in zurcido, appliqué, cross-stitch and lace, with tembleque headpieces.

label: Haute Couture & Fashion Design
defn: Dress designed by a named couturier or fashion house and shown in collections — haute couture (the Chambre Syndicale's protected label, from Worth in 1858) and designer ready-to-wear — placed by designer; the garments and collections are the works (Dior's New Look, 1947; Chanel's suit; Balenciaga's
aliases: couture; haute couture; fashion design; designer fashion

label: Dumbara Mats
defn: Hana-fibre mats with symbolic motifs woven by the kinnara community of the Dumbara valley in Sri Lanka (UNESCO 2021).

label: Noken
defn: Knotted and woven string bags of bark fibre and orchid stem made by women of Papua (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2012).

label: Daluang
defn: Javanese beaten-bark paper (dluwang) of paper mulberry, made in Ponorogo and Garut and used for pesantren and wayang beber manuscripts.

label: Kumihimo
defn: Japanese braided silk cords made on stands (marudai, takadai), for sword mounts, armour lacing and obijime.

label: Maedeup
defn: Korean decorative knotting in silk cord, with tassels for norigae pendants and ritual objects; makers designated maedeupjang.

label: Chaesang
defn: Korean boxes of dyed bamboo strips woven in patterns; makers designated chaesangjang.

label: Wanchojang
defn: Korean weaving of sedge (wanchoe) into patterned mats (hwamunseok), baskets and cushions, especially of Ganghwa island.

label: Ugandan Barkcloth
defn: Barkcloth beaten from the inner bark of the mutuba fig by Baganda craftsmen, terracotta-coloured, for royal and funerary use (UNESCO 2008).

label: Mbuti Barkcloth
defn: Barkcloth of the Mbuti of the Ituri forest, prepared by men and painted by women with linear and dotted designs in gardenia and charcoal.

label: Agaseke
defn: Coiled lidded baskets of Rwanda with conical lids and geometric patterns, made by women.

label: Panama Hat
defn: Hats plaited from toquilla palm straw in Ecuador (Montecristi, Cuenca), inscribed by UNESCO in 2012.

label: Pomo Basketry
defn: Coiled and twined baskets of the Pomo of northern California, among them the feathered and beaded gift baskets and the art baskets made for sale by named weavers.

label: California Indian Basketry
defn: Twined and coiled basketry of the Native peoples of California and the adjoining Great Basin edge other than the Pomo: Hupa, Karuk and Yurok overlay-twined caps, Yokuts bottleneck baskets, Cahuilla coiled baskets, Washoe degikup.

label: Spruce-Root Basketry
defn: Fine twined baskets and hats of split spruce root with false-embroidery grass designs, made by Tlingit and Haida women of the northern Northwest Coast.

label: Unangan Grass Basketry
defn: Very finely twined wild-rye-grass baskets, wallets and lidded jars of the Unangan (Aleut), above all the Attu baskets with silk false embroidery made for sale after 1867.

label: Plateau Cornhusk Bags
defn: Flat twined bags of Indian hemp with cornhusk false embroidery made by Nez Perce, Yakama, Umatilla and other Columbia Plateau women for root storage and exchange.

label: Plateau Imbricated Basketry
defn: Coiled cedar-root baskets imbricated with bear grass and cherry bark made by Klickitat, Nlaka'pamux and other Interior Salish weavers: berry baskets, lidded trunks.

label: Apache Basketry
defn: Coiled willow and devil's-claw ollas and trays and pitched twined water jars of the Western, Jicarilla and Mescalero Apache, with figures of people and animals.

label: Pima Basketry
defn: Coiled willow, cattail and devil's-claw baskets of the Akimel O'odham (Pima) and Tohono O'odham (Papago), the latter also in yucca and bear grass, with fret and squash-blossom designs.

label: Hopi Basketry
defn: Basketry of the Hopi mesas: coiled galleta-grass and yucca plaques of Second Mesa and wicker plaques of rabbitbrush of Third Mesa, often with katsina figures.

label: Rivercane Basketry
defn: Plaited baskets of split rivercane dyed with walnut and bloodroot, made by Cherokee, Chitimacha, Choctaw and Koasati weavers of the Southeast, including the double-woven baskets.

label: Wabanaki Basketry
defn: Woven brown-ash splint and braided sweetgrass baskets of the Wabanaki (Passamaquoddy, Penobscot, Maliseet, Mi'kmaq) of Maine and the Maritimes, from work baskets to fancy 'curly' baskets.

label: Birchbark Biting
defn: Designs bitten into thin folded sheets of birchbark by Anishinaabe, Cree and Algonquin women, used as patterns for quill and bead embroidery and as works in themselves.

label: Tapa Cloth
defn: Barkcloth beaten from paper-mulberry and other inner bark across the Pacific and painted, stencilled, rubbed or printed with designs: Samoan siapo, Tongan ngatu, Fijian masi, Hawaiian kapa, Niuean hiapo, Omie and Maisin barkcloth.

label: ʻIe Tōga
defn: The finely plaited pandanus fine mats of Samoa, and the fine mats of Tonga and Tuvalu, exchanged as the highest valuables at life-crisis ceremonies: ʻie tōga, Tongan kie and taʻovala.

label: Aboriginal Fibre Art
defn: The coiled, looped, twined and plaited fibre work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women and men, from string bags and baskets to contemporary fibre sculpture: dillybags, Arnhem Land pandanus baskets, rainforest bicornual baskets, Tjanpi grass sculpture, ghost-net sculpture.

label: Lalava
defn: Decorative coconut-fibre (sennit, magimagi) lashing of Tonga, Fiji and Samoa, binding the beams of houses and the hulls of canoes in red and black geometric patterns, now also made as freestanding works.

label: Sweetgrass Baskets
defn: Coiled baskets of sweetgrass, bulrush and pine needle sewn with palmetto by the Gullah Geechee of the South Carolina Lowcountry, a West African coiling tradition: fanner baskets, sewing baskets.

label: Panier de Mayun
defn: The willow and bramble baskets of Mayun in the Brière marshes (Loire-Atlantique).

label: Bastabinne
defn: Swedish baskets plaited from strips of spruce bast.

label: Birch-Bark Crafts
defn: Containers, boxes, footwear and objects of folded, woven, sewn and carved birch bark made across Finland, Karelia and Russia: tuohikontti backpacks, tuesok boxes, woven bast shoes.

label: Shemogodsk Carving
defn: Openwork carving of birch bark from the Shemoksa river near Veliky Ustyug since the early 19th century, called 'northern lace', on boxes and tuesoks.

label: Pärekori
defn: Finnish baskets plaited from pulled wood shingles (päre).
