defn: Petroglyphs pecked on the cliffs of the Helan and Yin mountains of Ningxia and Inner Mongolia, from the Neolithic to the medieval period: masks, animals and hunters (Helankou, Damaidi).

label: Saharan Rock Art
defn: Engraved and painted rock art of the Sahara from the Holocene to historical times, by stylistic phases: Bubaline engravings, Round Head paintings, Bovidian (pastoral) paintings, Dabous giraffes.

label: San Rock Art
defn: Painted and engraved rock art of the San (Bushmen) of southern Africa, over tens of thousands of years: Drakensberg eland paintings, Twyfelfontein engravings, Tsodilo paintings.

label: Sasanian Rock Reliefs
defn: Royal reliefs carved on cliff faces in Fars and western Iran by the Sasanian kings, 3rd–7th century, following Achaemenid precedent: Naqsh-e Rostam investitures, Bishapur triumph of Shapur I, Taq-e Bostan.

label: Hittite Rock Reliefs
defn: Reliefs of gods and kings carved on rock in Hittite Anatolia, 14th–13th century BC: Yazılıkaya, Fraktin, Hanyeri, Taşçı.

label: Gobustan Rock Art
defn: Petroglyphs of hunters, dancers, animals and reed boats pecked into the rocks of Gobustan in Azerbaijan from the late Upper Palaeolithic onward (UNESCO 2007).

label: Rock Art in the Hail Region
defn: Petroglyphs of humans, animals and inscriptions at Jubbah and Shuwaymis in the Ha'il region of Saudi Arabia, spanning some 10,000 years (UNESCO 2015).
aliases: Hail rock art;Jubbah and Shuwaymis petroglyphs

label: Cueva de las Manos
defn: Stencilled hands and hunting scenes of guanacos painted in the Río Pinturas caves of Patagonia from c. 9300 BP (UNESCO 1999).

label: Serra da Capivara Rock Art
defn: The painted rock shelters of Serra da Capivara (Piauí), with Nordeste-tradition hunting, dancing and sexual scenes (UNESCO 1991): Pedra Furada, Toca do Boqueirão.

label: Toro Muerto Petroglyphs
defn: Thousands of petroglyphs pecked on volcanic boulders at Toro Muerto (Arequipa) with dancers, camelids and birds, with related Andean sites: Toro Muerto, Toquepala Caves, Miculla.

label: Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
defn: Red-ochre paintings of jaguars, hunters and dancers on the tepuis of Chiribiquete in the Colombian Amazon (UNESCO 2018).

label: Pecos River Style
defn: Large polychrome pictographs of shamanic figures painted in the rock shelters of the Lower Pecos Canyonlands of Texas and Coahuila (c. 2700 BCE onward): White Shaman Shelter, Fate Bell Shelter, Panther Cave.

label: Barrier Canyon Style
defn: Archaic pictographs of tall tapering ghost-like figures on the Colorado Plateau of Utah: Great Gallery, Horseshoe Canyon, Sego Canyon.

label: Chumash Rock Painting
defn: Polychrome pictographs of circles, wheels and beings painted in caves of the Chumash territory of southern California (c. 1000–1800): Painted Cave, Painted Rock (Carrizo Plain), Burro Flats.

label: Coso Rock Art
defn: Petroglyphs of bighorn sheep, hunters and patterned-body figures in the Coso Range of the Mojave Desert, the largest concentration in North America.

label: Writing-on-Stone Rock Art
defn: Petroglyphs and pictographs of the Plains, incised in the sandstone of the Milk River valley, Alberta, including biographic warrior scenes (Áísínai'pi, UNESCO 2019).

label: Rock Paintings of the Sierra de San Francisco
defn: The Great Murals of Baja California: life-size red and black human and animal figures painted in the rock shelters of the Sierra de San Francisco and Sierra de Guadalupe (UNESCO 1993).

label: Arnhem Land Rock Art
defn: The painted rock shelters of the western Arnhem Land plateau and Kakadu, from Dynamic figures to the recent x-ray and contact paintings: Ubirr, Burrungkuy (Nourlangie), Nanguluwur, Injalak Hill.

label: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
defn: The fine-line figure paintings of the north-west Kimberley, slender tasselled human figures of great age.

label: Murujuga Rock Art
defn: The petroglyphs of the Burrup Peninsula and Dampier Archipelago (Murujuga), over a million engravings made across tens of thousands of years.

label: Sydney Rock Engravings
defn: The outline engravings on Hawkesbury sandstone in the Sydney basin: animals, ancestral beings and people: Ku-ring-gai Chase sites.

label: Quinkan Rock Art
defn: The painted shelters around Laura on Cape York with the Quinkan spirit figures.

label: Panaramitee Style
defn: The widespread Australian engraving style of tracks, circles and dots ('track and circle'), among the oldest rock art of the continent: Ewaninga, Panaramitee.

label: Māori Rock Art
defn: The charcoal and red-ochre drawings in limestone shelters of South Canterbury and North Otago: Takiroa, Awamoko.

label: Franco-Cantabrian Cave Art
defn: Upper Palaeolithic painted and engraved cave art of south-western France and northern Spain, c. 40,000–11,000 BP: Chauvet, Lascaux, Altamira, Font-de-Gaume.

label: Côa Valley and Siega Verde Rock Art
defn: Open-air Upper Palaeolithic engravings of animals on schist outcrops in the Côa valley (Portugal) and at Siega Verde (Spain), c. 25,000–10,000 BP: Canada do Inferno, Penascosa, Ribeira de Piscos.

label: Levantine Rock Art
defn: Post-Palaeolithic naturalistic rock painting of eastern Spain, c. 8000–3500 BC, with hunting, warfare and gathering scenes in shelters: Cova dels Cavalls, Roca dels Moros (Cogul), Valltorta.
aliases: Rock Art of the Mediterranean Basin on the Iberian Peninsula;Levantine art

label: Iberian Schematic Art
defn: Schematic rock painting and engraving of the Iberian peninsula, c. 5000–1000 BC, associated with the first farming and metal-using cultures: anthropomorphs and idols, Galician petroglyphs of Os Mouchos and Portela da Laxe.

label: Cup and Ring Marks
defn: Neolithic and Bronze Age carvings of cups and concentric rings on outcrops and standing stones of Atlantic Europe, above all Britain and Ireland: Cochno Stone, Achnabreck, Roughting Linn.

label: Rock Carvings in Tanum
defn: Bronze Age rock carvings of Bohuslän in western Sweden, c. 1700–500 BC, with ships, warriors, ploughing scenes and weddings: Vitlycke panel, Aspeberget, Fossum.

label: Rock Carvings at Alta
defn: Rock carvings of hunter-fisher communities at Alta in Finnmark, c. 5000 BC – AD 0, with reindeer, elk, boats and bear hunts: Hjemmeluft, Bergbukten, Amtmannsnes.

label: Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea
defn: Neolithic petroglyphs of Russian Karelia, c. 4000–2000 BC, on the shores of Lake Onega (swans, solar signs, the 'demon') and at Zalavruga on the White Sea (hunting and boat scenes).

label: Ural Pictograms
defn: Red-ochre rock paintings (pisanitsy) on river cliffs of the Urals, Neolithic to Iron Age, with animals, figures and signs: Ignatievskaya Cave, Tagil pisanitsa.

label: Rock Drawings in Valcamonica
defn: Petroglyphs of the Camunni in the Val Camonica (Lombardy), from the Epipalaeolithic to the Iron Age and beyond: Bedolina Map, Camunian rose, Naquane.

label: Umayyad Wall Painting
defn: the figural wall paintings of the Umayyad desert palaces, above all the bath of Qusayr 'Amra (8th century).

label: Persian Wall Painting
defn: the palace murals of Safavid and Qajar Iran (Chehel Sotoun, Ali Qapu, Hasht Behesht).

label: Al-Qatt Al-Asiri
defn: the geometric wall decoration painted by women inside the houses of the Asir region of Saudi Arabia (UNESCO 2017).

label: Ajanta Paintings
defn: Buddhist cave murals of Ajanta (2nd century BCE–5th century CE), the classical model for Indian wall painting: Padmapani, Mahajanaka Jataka.

label: Sigiriya Frescoes
defn: The 5th-century paintings of women on the rock face of Kashyapa's palace at Sigiriya.

label: Kerala Mural Painting
defn: Temple and palace murals of Kerala (9th–19th century) in five colours: Mattancherry Palace Ramayana, Padmanabhapuram murals.

label: Kandyan Period Painting
defn: Buddhist temple murals of the Kandyan kingdom (1592–1815) in red and yellow narrative registers: Dambulla cave paintings, Degaldoruwa jatakas.

label: Shekhawati Frescoes
defn: Painted havelis, temples and forts of Shekhawati in Rajasthan, 18th–20th century, mixing Rajput, colonial and popular imagery.

label: Pithora Painting
defn: Ritual wall paintings of horses and deities by the Rathwa and Bhil of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

label: Saura Painting
defn: Ritual wall paintings (ittal) of the Sora of Odisha dedicated to Idital.

label: Sohrai and Khovar Painting
defn: Harvest (sohrai) and marriage-chamber (khovar) wall paintings of Hazaribagh, Jharkhand.

label: Rangoli
defn: Ritual floor drawing in powder and rice paste across South Asia: kolam, alpana, kalamezhuthu.

label: Tibetan Buddhist Wall Paintings
defn: The secco murals of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and temples across the Himalaya, from the Kashmiri-style programmes of Tabo and Alchi to Shalu, the Gyantse Kumbum and Guge: Alchi Sumtsek, Tabo assembly hall, Shalu murals.

label: Dunhuang Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist cave temples of the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang (4th–14th century): Cave 217 Pure Land, Jataka narratives, donor portraits.

label: Kizil Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist caves of the kingdom of Kucha (Kizil, Kumtura and neighbouring sites), 4th–8th century, in rhomboid narrative grids and lapis blue: Cave of the Sixteen Sword-Bearers, Buddha in Nirvana.

label: Bezeklik Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Uyghur Buddhist caves of Bezeklik and the Turfan oasis (Qocho) under the Uyghur kingdom (9th–13th century): pranidhi scenes, Uyghur donor princes.
aliases: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves murals;Uyghur Buddhist wall painting

label: Sogdian Wall Painting
defn: The secular and religious murals of Sogdian houses, temples and palaces (5th–8th century) at Panjikent, Afrasiyab and Varakhsha: Rustam cycle, Hall of the Ambassadors, Red Hall of Varakhsha.

label: Bagan Murals
defn: The tempera wall paintings of the temples of Bagan (11th–13th century) and their Inwa and Konbaung successors: Abeyadana, Lokahteikpan Jatakas, Ananda temple.

label: Thai Mural Painting
defn: Tempera wall paintings of Thai Buddhist ordination halls and viharas, late Ayutthaya to early Rattanakosin and Lanna: Wat Phra Kaew Ramakien, Wat Pho, Wat Phumin, Wat Chong Nonsi.

label: Yongle Palace Murals
defn: The Daoist murals of the Yongle Palace in Shanxi (14th century), with the procession of deities in the Hall of Three Purities, and the Buddhist murals of the Fahai Temple near Beijing (1443).

label: Takamatsuzuka Tomb Murals
defn: Painted plaster walls of the late 7th-century tombs of Asuka (Takamatsuzuka and Kitora), with court ladies, the Four Directional Animals and star charts.

label: Goguryeo Tomb Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Goguryeo tombs near Pyongyang and Ji'an (4th–7th century): hunting scenes, dancers and the Four Guardians (UNESCO 2004).

label: Dancheong
defn: Korean polychrome painting of wooden buildings, temples and palaces in blue, red, yellow, white and black patterns; masters designated dancheongjang.

label: Ethiopian Church Painting
defn: Wall painting of Ethiopian churches, on plaster and on canvas glued to walls: Debre Berhan Selassie ceiling of winged faces, Lake Tana monastery murals, Lalibela paintings.

label: Litema
defn: Incised and painted mud-wall decoration of Basotho homesteads in Lesotho and the Free State, renewed by women.

label: Ndebele House Painting
defn: Geometric mural painting of the Southern Ndebele of South Africa on homestead walls, by women (Esther Mahlangu).

label: Imigongo
defn: Rwandan relief panels of cow dung in black, white and red spirals and zigzags, from house walls to boards.

label: Egyptian Tomb Painting
defn: Wall painting in the tombs and temples of pharaonic Egypt, in tempera on plaster: Meidum Geese, Tomb of Nebamun, Tomb of Nefertari, Theban nobles' tombs.

label: Minoan Wall Painting
defn: Fresco painting of Bronze Age Crete and the Minoanised Aegean, c. 1700–1450 BC: Bull-Leaping Fresco from Knossos, Akrotiri Spring Fresco, Fisherman of Thera.
aliases: Minoan frescoes;Aegean wall painting;Wall Paintings of Thera

label: Etruscan Tomb Painting
defn: Painted chamber tombs of Etruria, 7th–2nd century BC, chiefly at Tarquinia and Cerveteri: Tomb of the Leopards, Tomb of the Triclinium, François Tomb at Vulci.

label: Ancient Greek Painting
defn: Surviving Greek wall painting, mostly from tombs of the 5th–3rd century BC in Macedonia, Thrace and Magna Graecia: Tomb of Philip II at Vergina, Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak, Tomb of the Diver at Paestum.

label: Pompeian Wall Painting
defn: Roman wall painting of the Vesuvian cities and Rome, classed by August Mau in four Pompeian Styles, 2nd century BC – AD 79: Villa of the Mysteries, Villa of Poppaea at Oplontis, House of the Vettii.

label: Catacomb Painting
defn: Early Christian and Jewish funerary and devotional wall painting of the 2nd–5th century, above all in the catacombs of Rome and at Dura-Europos: Catacomb of Priscilla, Via Latina catacomb, Dura-Europos synagogue.

label: Byzantine Wall Painting
defn: Fresco programmes of Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches, 6th–15th century: Cappadocian rock-cut churches, painted churches of Troödos, Panselinos at the Protaton, Mystras.

label: Faras Wall Paintings
defn: Wall paintings of the cathedral of Faras in the Nubian kingdom of Makuria, 8th–14th century, removed in 1961–64 to Warsaw and Khartoum: Bishop Petros with St Peter, Saint Anne, Nativity.

label: Maya Mural Painting
defn: The wall paintings of the Maya from the Preclassic to the Postclassic: San Bartolo murals, Bonampak Room 2 battle, Calakmul market murals.

label: Teotihuacan Mural Painting
defn: The fresco painting of the apartment compounds of Teotihuacan (c. 200–650 CE): Tepantitla Great Goddess, Tetitla, Atetelco.

label: Cacaxtla Murals
defn: The Epiclassic murals of Cacaxtla (Tlaxcala, c. 650–900 CE), mixing Maya and central Mexican styles: Battle Mural, Bird Man.

label: Moche Murals
defn: Painted and modelled mud-plaster friezes of Moche temples: Huaca de la Luna Ai Apaec friezes, El Brujo.

label: Mexican Muralism
defn: The public mural movement of post-revolutionary Mexico (1920s–1970s) led by Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros: Rivera's National Palace murals, Orozco's Hospicio Cabañas, Siqueiros' Polyforum.

label: Chilean Muralism
defn: Chilean public mural painting from the 1940s, from Siqueiros' Chillán murals to the brigade painting of the Brigada Ramona Parra.

label: Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua
defn: Public murals painted in Sandinista Nicaragua (1979–1990) by Nicaraguan and international brigades.

label: Romanesque Wall Painting
defn: Fresco programmes of Romanesque churches, c. 1000–1200: Sant Climent de Taüll, Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, San Isidoro, León, Sant'Angelo in Formis.

label: Gothic Wall Painting
defn: Wall painting in Gothic churches and palaces, 13th–15th century, north of the Alps and in the Adriatic: Albi Cathedral, Saint-Sernin, Beram and Hrastovlje Danse macabre, Albertus Pictor's Swedish churches.

label: Painted Churches of Northern Moldavia
defn: The 15th–16th-century churches of Bukovina painted inside and out with Byzantine-derived cycles under Stephen the Great and Petru Rareș: Voroneț Last Judgement, Humor, Sucevița, Moldovița.

label: Scottish Renaissance Painted Ceilings
defn: Tempera-painted timber ceilings of Scottish houses and castles, c. 1550–1650, with emblems, grotesques and heraldry: Prestongrange, Aberdour Castle, Culross Palace.

label: Murals in Northern Ireland
defn: Loyalist and republican political murals painted on gable walls in Northern Ireland since the early 20th century and above all from the 1970s: Falls Road murals, Bogside Artists, King Billy murals.

label: Samchyky Painting
defn: The decorative painting of the walls and interiors of houses in Samchyky village (Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine), with unique floral patterns.

label: Illusionistic Ceiling Painting
defn: Ceiling and vault painting in fresco that opens the architecture to a painted sky by foreshortening (di sotto in sù) and painted architecture (quadratura), from Mantegna to the Baroque and Rococo: Mantegna's Camera degli Sposi oculus, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling, Pozzo's Sant'Ignazio, Tiep
aliases: quadratura;di sotto in sù;sotto in su;Baroque ceiling painting

label: Italian Renaissance Fresco
defn: The fresco cycles painted on the walls and vaults of Italian chapels, churches and palaces from Giotto to the High Renaissance, studied where they stand: Arena (Scrovegni) Chapel, Brancacci Chapel, Sistine Chapel ceiling, Raphael Rooms.

label: Street Art
defn: Unsanctioned and commissioned art in public space from the 1970s: graffiti writing, stencil, paste-up and mural: Banksy's Girl with Balloon, Os Gêmeos's murals, JR's Women Are Heroes.

label: Umayyad Mosaics
defn: the glass wall mosaics of the Dome of the Rock and the Great Mosque of Damascus (7th–8th century), made by Byzantine-trained craftsmen.

label: Zellige
defn: geometric mosaic of hand-cut glazed tiles set in plaster, the wall and floor revetment of Morocco and al-Andalus.

label: Moʿaraq (Cut-Tile Mosaic)
defn: the tile revetment of Iranian and Central Asian architecture: cut-tile mosaic (mo'arraq) of the Timurid and Safavid periods, haft-rangi (seven-colour) tiles and banna'i brick-and-tile.

label: Kashi Kari
defn: the tile-mosaic revetment of Mughal and Punjabi buildings (Lahore, Multan, Thatta).

label: Aina-kari
defn: mirror mosaic: cut mirror glass set in plaster on walls and ceilings of Iranian palaces and shrines.

label: Hellenistic Mosaics
defn: Greek floor mosaics from the 5th to the 1st century BC, from pebble mosaics to tessellated opus vermiculatum: Pella stag hunt, Alexander Mosaic, Sosos's unswept floor.

label: Roman Mosaics
defn: Floor and wall mosaics of the Roman world, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, with strong regional schools in North Africa, Antioch and Sicily: Nile mosaic of Palestrina, Antioch mosaics, Villa Romana del Casale, Bardo mosaics.

label: Byzantine Mosaics
defn: Glass and stone wall mosaics of Byzantine churches and of the workshops they trained, 5th–14th century: San Vitale, Ravenna, Hagia Sophia, Daphni and Hosios Loukas, Monreale, San Marco.

label: Azulejo
defn: Painted tin-glazed tile panels covering walls of churches, palaces and streets in Portugal, Spain and Brazil from the 16th century: Palace of the Marquises of Fronteira, São Bento station, Valencian ceramic retables.

label: Trencadís
defn: Mosaic of broken tile and crockery shards laid on curved surfaces, the cladding of Catalan Modernisme (Gaudí, Jujol): Park Güell, Casa Batlló, Hospital de Sant Pau.

label: Portuguese Pavement
defn: Patterned pavement of black basalt and white limestone setts laid by hand in Portugal and its former colonies since the 19th century: Rossio waves, Copacabana promenade.

label: Soviet Mosaics
defn: Monumental mosaics on public buildings, metro stations and housing of the Soviet Union and its republics, 1920s–1991, a state programme of monumental art: Kyiv and Donetsk school mosaics, Yerevan facade mosaics.

label: Steppe Geoglyphs
defn: The earthen and stone ground figures of the Turgai Trough in northern Kazakhstan (Neolithic–Iron Age), at least 260 squares, rings and crosses: Ushtogay Square, Turgay triradial swastika.

label: Gozan no Okuribi
defn: The five bonfire characters and figures (Daimonji, Myōhō, the boat and the torii) lit on the hills around Kyoto on 16 August, laid out as fixed hillside figures.

label: Nazca Lines
defn: Geoglyphs scraped into the desert of the Nazca and Palpa pampas (c. 500 BCE–500 CE), with straight lines and animal figures (UNESCO 1994): Hummingbird, Monkey, Condor, Palpa figures.

label: Pintados Geoglyphs
defn: Hillside geoglyphs of the Atacama made by removing or piling stones (c. 600–1500 CE): Cerro Pintados panels, Atacama Giant, Chug-Chug.

label: Acre Geoglyphs
defn: Geometric ditched enclosures of the south-western Amazon (Acre, Brazil), c. 0–1300 CE.

label: Effigy Mounds
defn: Earthen mounds raised in the shapes of animals and serpents in the Eastern Woodlands: Serpent Mound, the bear and bird mounds of Effigy Mounds National Monument.

label: Blythe Intaglios
defn: Giant human and animal figures scraped into the desert pavement near Blythe on the lower Colorado River.

label: Hill Figures
defn: Figures cut into hillsides to expose the chalk or limestone beneath, mainly in southern England, from the Bronze Age (Uffington) to the 18th–19th-century white horses: Uffington White Horse, Cerne Abbas Giant, Long Man of Wilmington.

label: Deq
defn: the facial and hand tattooing of Kurdish, Arab and Amazigh women.

label: Godna
defn: Tattooing of the tribal communities of central and eastern India (Baiga, Gond, Oraon), also transferred to painting on paper.

label: Mehndi
defn: Henna body painting of South Asia for weddings and festivals.

label: Sak Yant
defn: Thai, Khmer, Lao and Burmese protective yantra tattooing of sacred diagrams and Khom script, applied by monks and ajarn with a steel rod.

label: Mentawai Tattooing
defn: The full-body line tattooing (titi) of the Mentawai of Siberut, west of Sumatra.

label: Batok
defn: The traditional tattooing of the Philippines, from the Visayan pintados to the Kalinga and Bontoc warrior tattoos.

label: Irezumi
defn: Japanese tattooing, above all the Edo-period full-body designs inspired by ukiyo-e heroes, with the Okinawan women's hand tattoos (hajichi) and Ainu lip tattoos as kinds.

label: African Scarification
defn: Cicatrisation and keloid scarification as body art across Africa, with named regional marks: Yoruba facial marks (ila), Nuba and Dinka marks.

label: Kakiniit
defn: Inuit women's facial and body tattooing, sewn or pricked with soot-blackened sinew, revived in Nunavut and Greenland since the 2000s.

label: Tā Moko
defn: Māori tattooing, chiselled (uhi) into the skin in curvilinear designs that mark descent and rank: moko on men's faces, moko kauae for women.

label: Polynesian Tattooing
defn: The tattoo traditions of Polynesia worked with toothed combs and a mallet: Samoan peʻa and malu, Marquesan full-body tattoo, Tahitian tatau, Fijian veiqia.

label: Sailor Tattoos
defn: The Western tattoo tradition of sailors and its prison and street derivatives, which grew into the American traditional style of bold outlines and limited colour (Sailor Jerry): swallows, anchors, pin-ups.

label: Sona
defn: Sand drawings (lusona, pl. sona) of the Chokwe and neighbouring peoples of eastern Angola: continuous lines around a grid of dots, illustrating stories.

label: Navajo Sandpainting
defn: Dry paintings of coloured sands, pollen and charcoal made by Diné medicine men for healing chants and erased after use, and their permanent versions glued on board for sale since the 1930s.

label: Corpus Christi Flower Carpets
defn: Carpets of flowers laid on the streets of Polish villages (Spycimierz and others) for the Corpus Christi processions (UNESCO 2021).
aliases: Flower carpets tradition for Corpus Christi processions

label: Installation Art
defn: Art that makes or transforms a space to be entered or experienced, from the 1960s: Kabakov's The Man Who Flew into Space, Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms.

label: Conceptual Art
defn: Art since the mid-1960s in which the idea is the work: Kosuth's One and Three Chairs, Sol LeWitt's Wall Drawings, On Kawara's Date Paintings.

label: Fluxus
defn: The international intermedia network of the 1960s around George Maciunas: event scores, actions and multiples: Yoko Ono's Cut Piece, Fluxkits.

label: Mail Art
defn: Art sent and exchanged through the postal system from the 1960s (Ray Johnson's New York Correspondence School): Johnson's moticos, artistamps.

label: Arte Povera
defn: The Italian movement (1967) of "poor" materials and process: Pistoletto's Venus of the Rags, Merz's igloos, Kounellis's live horses.

label: Land Art
defn: Art made in and of the landscape from the late 1960s: Smithson's Spiral Jetty, De Maria's Lightning Field, Goldsworthy's works.

label: Viennese Actionism
defn: The radical Austrian performance movement of the 1960s: Nitsch's Orgien Mysterien Theater, Schwarzkogler's actions.

label: Performance Art
defn: Art made by the artist's live action before an audience, from the 1960s: Abramović's Rhythm 0, Beuys's I Like America and America Likes Me.

label: Relational art
defn: Art of the 1990s whose material is human relations and their social context, theorised by Nicolas Bourriaud in Relational Aesthetics (1998): Tiravanija's cooked meals, Gillick's discussion platforms, Höller's slides.

label: Generative Art
defn: Art made wholly or partly by an autonomous system — an algorithm, program or machine — from the plotter drawings of the 1960s computer-art pioneers to code-based generative work: Nees's Schotter, Molnár's (Dés)Ordres, Mohr's P-197, Casey Reas's Process works.

label: Internet Art
defn: Art made for and distributed through the Internet from the mid-1990s (net.art), its browser, e-mail and website works and the post-internet generation: Lialina's My Boyfriend Came Back from the War, JODI's wwwwwwwww.jodi.org, Ćosić's ASCII History of Moving Images.
aliases: net art;net.art;web art;NFT art;crypto art;pixel art

label: AI Art
defn: Art made with machine-learning and other AI systems, from Harold Cohen's AARON (1973) to GAN and diffusion-model works: Cohen's AARON drawings, Klingemann's Memories of Passersby I, Anadol's Unsupervised, Ridler's Mosaic Virus.

label: Video Art
defn: Art made with video from the mid-1960s: Nam June Paik's TV Buddha, Bill Viola's The Crossing, Joan Jonas's Vertical Roll.

label: New Media Art
defn: Art made with digital, networked and computational technologies: Cory Arcangel's Super Mario Clouds, Rafael Lozano-Hemmer's Pulse Room.

label: Thonet Bentwood Furniture
defn: Steam-bent beechwood furniture made in series by Gebrüder Thonet (Vienna, from 1849) and its rivals such as J. & J. Kohn, including bentwood designs by Vienna architects: the No. 14 chair, Hoffmann's Sitzmaschine, Otto Wagner's Postsparkasse chair.

label: De Stijl Design
defn: Furniture, lighting and graphics of the Dutch De Stijl group (1917–1931), built from primary colours and rectilinear elements: Rietveld's Red and Blue Chair, Zig-Zag Chair, hanging lamp, the De Stijl magazine.

label: Bauhaus Design
defn: Prototypes for industry from the Bauhaus workshops (Weimar 1919, Dessau 1925, Berlin 1932–33) and their makers: tubular-steel chairs, metal-workshop lamps and tea wares, weaving-workshop textiles. See also I3-17 Bauhaus.

label: Union des Artistes Modernes
defn: French modernist design of the Union des Artistes Modernes (founded 1929) and its postwar heirs: tubular-steel and sheet-metal furniture and lighting for serial production by Le Corbusier, Perriand, Gray, Prouvé and Mouille.

label: American Mid-Century Modern Design
defn: American furniture, lighting and housewares for serial production c. 1940–1970, led by Herman Miller and Knoll and the Cranbrook circle: Eames chairs, Saarinen's Tulip chair, Bertoia's Diamond chair, Nelson's Ball Clock.

label: Danish Modern
defn: Danish furniture and lighting c. 1925–1975 held by design museums as a national school: the Klint school of cabinetmaking, the Cabinetmakers' Guild exhibitions and industrial chairs and lamps by Jacobsen, Wegner, Henningsen, Kjærholm and Juhl.

label: Italian Modern Design
defn: Postwar Italian industrial design c. 1945–1980 (the 'bel design' celebrated in MoMA's Italy: The New Domestic Landscape, 1972): Milan furniture, lighting, appliances and office machines by Ponti, the Castiglionis, Zanuso, Magistretti, Sapper and Olivetti.

label: British Modern Design
defn: British modern furniture, lighting, textiles and industrial design for serial production c. 1930–1975, from Isokon and the Anglepoise to the Festival of Britain 'Contemporary' style and Design Council-era products.

label: Pop Design
defn: Furniture, lighting and products of the 1960s Pop and Space Age: injection-moulded plastics, inflatables, foam and bright colour, by Panton, Aarnio, Paulin, Colombo, Mourgue and Zanotta's bean-bag.

label: Radical Design
defn: Italian Radical or Anti-design (c. 1966–1980): Florentine and Turin groups and Studio Alchimia that attacked good-taste modernism through ironic, conceptual furniture: Archizoom, Superstudio, Gruppo Strum, Gufram, Gaetano Pesce.

label: Memphis Group
defn: Furniture, lighting and objects of the Milan collective Memphis (1981–1988) led by Ettore Sottsass: plastic laminates, clashing colour and pattern, international contributors.

label: Dutch Design
defn: Dutch furniture, lighting and product design held as a national school: the postwar Goed Wonen movement, the conceptual Droog Design collective (1993) and the 'Dutch Design' generation it launched.

label: Wiener Werkstätte
defn: Objects of the Vienna workshop cooperative Wiener Werkstätte (1903–1932) founded by Josef Hoffmann, Koloman Moser and Fritz Waerndorfer: geometric silver and metalwork, furniture, ceramics, textiles, postcards and fashion made in series.

label: Deutscher Werkbund
defn: Industrial design of the Deutscher Werkbund (founded Munich 1907), the association of artists, architects and industry for quality mass production: Peter Behrens's AEG products, Riemerschmid's machine furniture, the Frankfurt Kitchen.

label: Streamline Moderne
defn: The streamlined styling of the first American industrial designers c. 1930–1955: appliances, radios, telephones and trains shaped by Loewy, Dreyfuss, Bel Geddes, Teague and Deskey for Depression-era mass production.

label: Ulm School and Braun Functionalism
defn: Systematic functionalist product design of the Hochschule für Gestaltung Ulm (1953–1968) and Braun under Dieter Rams, the core of West German 'Gute Form': SK 4, T3 radio, 606 shelving, Ulm stool.

label: Scandinavian Modern
defn: Nordic applied and industrial design c. 1930–1980 (the 'Design in Scandinavia' exhibitions, 1954–57): glass, ceramics, silver, textiles and products from Arabia, Iittala, Orrefors, Marimekko, Georg Jensen and Bang & Olufsen. Danish furniture: Danish Modern.
aliases: Swedish Modern; Nordic design; Design in Scandinavia

label: Japanese Industrial Design
defn: Postwar Japanese industrial and product design held by design museums as a school, joining craft tradition and mass production: Sori Yanagi, Kenji Ekuan's GK Design, Sony and Muji, Kuramata and Fukasawa.

label: Automobile Design
defn: Car and motorcycle bodies designed for series production and held by design collections as landmarks (MoMA's 8 Automobiles, 1951): Italian carrozzeria (Pininfarina, Bertone, Italdesign, Zagato), German, French and American styling studios.

label: Postmodern Design
defn: Postmodern product and furniture design c. 1978–1995: Alessi's architect-designed housewares, London's Creative Salvage and one-off makers, Starck and the international designer-object (V&A, Postmodernism: Style and Subversion, 2011).

label: Contemporary Industrial Design
defn: Product, furniture and lighting design for industrial production since c. 1990 collected by design museums: minimal 'Super Normal' objects, ergonomic office seating, digital and new-material design, critical design.

label: Art Deco Poster
defn: Commercial and travel posters of the 1920s–30s in Art Deco and Cubist-derived styles, printed by lithography for railways, liners and brands: Cassandre, Carlu, Colin, Loupot, McKnight Kauffer.

label: Constructivist Graphic Design
defn: Soviet and Central European Constructivist posters, books and magazines c. 1919–1935 built from photomontage, bold sans-serif type and diagonal composition: Lissitzky, Rodchenko, the Stenberg brothers, Klutsis. See also B2-11 Soviet Poster.

label: New Typography
defn: Die neue Typographie of the 1920s–30s: asymmetric, sans-serif, photo-typographic layouts for advertising and print by Tschichold, the Bauhaus typographers, the ring neue werbegestalter and Dutch and Czech practitioners.

label: Isotype
defn: The International System of Typographic Picture Education, pictorial statistics developed at the Vienna Gesellschafts- und Wirtschaftsmuseum from 1925 by Otto Neurath, Marie Neurath and Gerd Arntz.

label: Swiss Style (International Typographic Style)
defn: Swiss graphic design of the 1950s–60s from the Zurich and Basel schools: grid-based layout, sans-serif type, objective photography and asymmetric posters, spread internationally as the International Typographic Style.

label: New York School (graphic design)
defn: American modernist graphic design c. 1940–1970 centred on New York (Meggs's 'New York School'): playful, conceptual adaptations of European modernism in advertising, book jackets, logos and film titles by Rand, Lustig, Thompson, Bass.

label: Corporate Identity Design
defn: Programmatic visual identities for companies, transport systems and Olympic Games from the 1950s: logos, pictograms and design manuals by Pentagram, Unimark, Henrion, Aicher, Wyman and Design Research Unit.

label: Push Pin Studios
defn: The New York studio founded in 1954 by Seymour Chwast, Milton Glaser and Edward Sorel, whose eclectic, historicist illustration-led graphics and Push Pin Graphic broke with Swiss modernism.

label: Psychedelic Poster Art
defn: Concert and counterculture posters of 1966–1970 printed for San Francisco's Fillmore and Avalon ballrooms and London's UFO Club: vibrating colour, Art Nouveau lettering, by the San Francisco Big Five and Hapshash and the Coloured Coat.

label: Album Cover Design
defn: Record-sleeve design for mass-pressed LPs and singles from 1940, collected by MoMA and the V&A: Blue Note jazz sleeves, rock and psychedelic covers, punk and post-punk graphics.

label: Japanese Graphic Design
defn: Postwar Japanese graphic design: Olympic and corporate posters of the Nippon Design Center generation, the 1960s avant-garde of Yokoo, advertising art direction, and digital pictograms such as the first emoji.

label: Dutch Graphic Design
defn: Postwar Dutch graphic design held as a national school: Sandberg's Stedelijk catalogues, Wim Crouwel and Total Design, PTT and banknote design, and the book designers of the Dutch Design era.

label: New Wave Typography
defn: Postmodern graphic design from the 1970s: the Basel 'Swiss Punk' of Weingart and his students, Cranbrook and Emigre in the United States, British style-magazine typography and the digital-era designer-authors.
